# Archetype forensic audit 4: every archetype, every perspective, under the gate rule

Scope: all 214 archetypes in `archetype_tags.py`, audited by seven independent reviewers against the post-audit-3 engine, the source documents, the prior audits and the FMP catalogue, on a 12-point checklist (spirit fidelity, gate legitimacy, lineage, reach, missing-data direction, units and currency, definitions, code correctness, regression, tiers and weights, overlap, and the three new data layers). No back-testing or statistics.

## The gate rule (user)
A gate stays only if it is explicitly part of the archetype's thesis, a number the archetype's own source states, or a data-validity guard. Any other fixed threshold is arbitrary: it is removed as a gate and, where it carries information, becomes a weight blended into the archetype's spirit score (`_DEMOTED`, 25% by default, per-archetype where the user asks for more). The spirit score ranks members and sets the exceptional (top quarter) and elite (top tenth) tiers.

## What changed (commits on the branch, in order)
- `acb562b`, `625c104`: three new global layers and their wiring. Universe-wide EPS surprise history (`esb_*`, 17,513 names) behind the event fields and the master's beat fields; per-share compounding history (`fg_*`, 30,932 names) in Lynch growth, CANSLIM A, lindy growth, book compounding and the dilution checks, plus `per_share_compounder_flag`; the dated EV series (`evh_*`, 28,048 names) as the primary multiple-compression read.
- `39fc934`: the fallen-angel leverage leg removed (it had dropped III.BK at 3.96x with no loss year in eight).
- `c99761f`: the non-thesis gates removed across the engine and registered as weights (leverage caps, Altman vetoes, non-thesis dilution caps, tape cut-offs, invented quality floors).
- `717df6a`, `b140bbf`, `b4d4c84`: XR slice A. All XR leverage caps become weights; the cannibal buyback leg reads the global FY repurchase yield (it had made both cannibal gates US-only); the negative-EBITDA trough keeps the net-cash sign as its protection with the size of net cash and debt/assets as a 50% weight.
- `11a1f3b`: multibagger slice A. The single-purchase insider bypass closed; observed-uncovered includes names with no rating coverage but a real earnings record; the pre-revenue biotech branch reads R&D growth; the fallen deep-value subsets counted once; survivor and per-share weights.
- `3d07022`: multibagger slice B. fallen_less_than_industry_financed revived (it fired on nobody); a buyback is not an informed-buyer arrival; the quality-at-distress product bounds aligned; a contradicting lens dropped.
- `f5f74ba`: XR slice B and singles slice A. The data-quality flag is computed before its fourteen readers (it had been a silent no-op); the last two leftover leverage caps and an over-tight profit leg become weights; weights for the facts the de-gating had orphaned.
- `1f9cd7c`: singles slice B. A qarp code bug (104 names wrongly excluded); the sources' own numbers on strong_coverage (debt/EBITDA 4x), owner_operator (58%), sustainable_scaler (<$300M, EV/S < 3, growth >= 25% as core) and levered_inflection (ND/EBITDA 1.5-3x as core).
- `879942d`: named-investor slice. Missing-data direction fixed on capital_discipline and Cundill; capital_discipline's tape and Yartseva cuts removed; cash_quality's double-duty cut removed; BAB leverage caps, the NAV-discount debt cap, and three orphaned legs become weights; Greenblatt's core is his own combined rank.

## Deliberately not changed
- Liquidity floors (standing instruction: denote liquidity, never filter on it).
- The dividend-veto direction where a blank almost always means no dividend.
- Count-hygiene clustering of tree_recipe with tree_recipe_10x (60% shared members): a judgment call left to the user.
- Wrong-date items that need new data rather than a rule change: post_reorg's emergence-date yield, a global consensus-revision series for cheap_growth_targets_up, observed coverage from analyst estimates.

### arch_mb_fallen_deep_value
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_LATENT_CLUSTERS.md conjunction "fallen_angel + deep_value" (2.49x fit / 3.37x test) and MULTIBAGGER_ARCHETYPES.md 10x patterns; Wolf Archetype 10 "Distressed / Deep-Value" (crash > 50%, P/B < 0.5, identifiable assets, a plausible path); Yartseva high B/M near lows. The thesis is a pure two-fact conjunction: far below the 5y high, and cheap on at least one absolute multiple.
- As coded (l.7461): `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _mb_deep`, where `_mb_fallen = ts_dist_hi260<=0.40` and `_mb_deep = (ev_ebit in (0,6]) | (pb in (0,0.7]) | (p_s in (0,0.3])` (l.7475-7478), all `.fillna(False)`. Lenses (11, dump3): dist_hi260(-), ev_ebit(-), pb(-), fcf_yield(+), mcap(-), 13D recency(+), rel_ind_ev_ebit(-), vs_ind_dist_hi260(-), and three audit-3 additions: `ts_wks_since_lo260`(-, fresh low), `ncav_pct_mcap`(+, asset floor), `fmp_altman_z`(+, "not too far gone"). 854 firers (archetype_tags.csv, verified), 20 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: the three audit-3 lens additions landed exactly as suggested (ranked #1 in the audit-3 report) and correctly as LENSES, not gates — per the USER RULE this is the right placement since none of the three (fresh low, NCAV floor, Altman) is a number the source states; `fmp_altman_z` in particular was explicitly named a candidate GATE in audit-3 ("as a soft veto") and the engine correctly kept it out of the core. Count is unchanged from audit-3 (854 = 854): no collapse, no widening, exactly as expected since the core itself was not touched.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `_mb_deep` mixes an earnings multiple (EV/EBIT<=6, requires EBIT>0) with two multiples that admit LOSS-MAKERS (PB, PS have no profitability requirement): a member can be "deep value" purely on P/S<=0.3 while EBIT is negative, and the archetype does not say which branch fired, so a cheap earner and a cheap shell are the same tag. This was already flagged in audit-3 (methodology b) and remains true; suggestion #2 there ("surface `mb_deep_branch`") did not land — no such column exists in the dump3 lens block or in `archetype_tags.csv`'s column list.
  2. [count hygiene, USER RULE-adjacent] As established in the shared header: `arch_mb_fallen_value_turn` (302 firers) and `arch_mb_fallen_value_accel` (118 firers) are algebraic subsets of this archetype (100% of each also fires here, verified) — they add the SAME `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _mb_deep` core plus one extra AND-clause. `archetype_count` (l.9394-9431) counts all three independently because none of the three is in `_DEDUP_CLUSTERS`, so a name meeting the narrowest condition (e.g. value_turn) is credited with 2-3 "confirmations" of one underlying fact (fallen + deep). `arch_mb_fallen_stressed`, `arch_mb_fallen_insider`, and `arch_mb_fallen_trough` are NOT literal subsets (each swaps in an independent third fact — stress, insiders, or trough-acceleration) so they are legitimately separate confirmations and should stay uncounted-together.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5` (fg_*, global, ~30.9k names) as a through-cycle FCF-quality lens alongside `fcf_yield`, since a snapshot FCF yield can be a one-quarter accident; `evh_evs_vs_med_3y <= -0.30` (evh_*, currently only ~1,000/46,526 names, so treat as a corroborating lens only, not a leg, until the file's reach grows) as the own-history version of the cross-sector `p_s`/`pb` cheapness the core uses.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Add `mb_deep_branch` (categorical: which of EV/EBIT, PB, PS fired) alongside the flag, so a books consumer can separate the profitable-cheap case from the loss-making-cheap case without re-deriving it.
  2. [method] Add `arch_mb_fallen_value_turn` and `arch_mb_fallen_value_accel` to a `_DEDUP_CLUSTERS` entry with `arch_mb_fallen_deep_value` (parent counts once regardless of how many of its own AND-refinements also fire); do not add `fallen_stressed`/`fallen_insider`/`fallen_trough` to that cluster since they are not literal subsets.

### arch_mb_fallen_value_turn
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_LATENT_CLUSTERS.md "deep_value + fallen_angel + turnaround" (2.73x/3.60x); archetype_compendium Part II-B Andreola ("the first profitable quarter is the strongest footprint"); Wolf Archetype 9 Turnaround. Adds a recency-sensitive profit-turn fact to fallen_deep_value.
- As coded (l.7462): `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _mb_deep & _mb_turn`. `_mb_turn` (l.7479-7483) is an OR of seven flags from four sources (fqx_eps_turned, bs_ebit_turned, ebitda/ni/fcf_first_positive>0, fmp_dyn_opinc/ni_turned_positive) **AND-gated with recency**: `_mb_turn = _mb_turn & ((fqx_m_since_turn_positive<=12) | fqx_m_since_turn_positive.isna())` (l.7483). 302 firers, 22% US (domicile).
- Regression check: the audit-3 recency fix landed and is the whole story of this archetype's count movement: 422 (audit-3) -> 302 now (-28%), exactly consistent with adding the 12-month window; verified this is not over-tightening but the source's own stated window (the study's runs begin ~12 months after the turn). The NaN branch of the recency AND (`| isna()`) means a name whose `fqx_m_since_turn_positive` was never computed (e.g., the turn flag that fired was `bs_ebit_turned` or `fmp_dyn_*`, which do not feed that dating column) still passes with NO recency check at all — so the "recent" fix is enforced only for the sub-population where the dating column happens to be populated. Audit-3 suggestion #2 ("emit `mb_turn_source`") did NOT land: `archetype_tags.csv` has no such column and the lens list is unchanged from the audit-3 dump, so it is still impossible to tell an EBITDA-only turn from an EPS turn.
- Methodology issues:
  1. Recency is real for only part of the OR (see above): an `fmp_dyn_ni_turned_positive==1` name and a `bs_ebit_turned==1` name (base_snapshot, no per-quarter date) both bypass the 12-month test whenever `fqx_m_since_turn_positive` is NaN for them, which is likely whenever the turn was NOT on the FMP quarterly panel's own EBIT/EPS lines. This is a missing-data direction issue: NaN on the recency column PASSES, which is the friendly-to-firing direction, not the conservative one, for a leg whose entire audit-3 justification was "don't count an old flip."
  2. [count hygiene] 100% subset of `arch_mb_fallen_deep_value` (verified via pandas); see the header/parent section — should be in the same `_DEDUP_CLUSTERS` entry.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_ni_ps_3y > 0` or `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5 > 0` (fg_*, global) as a corroborating "the turn held for a full FY" lens, since the core's turn flags are all single-quarter or TTM snapshots; `esb_react_last` (esb_*, 17,513 names) as the "the market has not yet priced this turn" perception lens the source's Andreola footprint implies but the core omits.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Require the recency test on EVERY OR-branch of `_mb_turn`, not just the branches that happen to populate `fqx_m_since_turn_positive`; where a branch has no native date (bs_ebit_turned, fmp_dyn_*), read its own nearest date proxy (fmp_dyn_* already carries "latest quarter positive, prior 4 not" — cap it structurally at <=4 quarters instead of falling through to the unconditional pass).
  2. [method] Emit `mb_turn_source` (which of the seven flags fired) as the audit-3 suggestion asked; needed to separate an EBITDA-sign-flip member from an EPS-turn member for anyone reading the book.
  3. [method] Join the `_DEDUP_CLUSTERS` entry proposed under fallen_deep_value.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — turnaround fact present but heterogeneously defined (issue 1). 2 gates — `_mb_deep`/`_mb_fallen` are the study's numbers; the 12-month window is the source's own timing claim (Andreola/FORENSICS), so it is a legitimate thesis-derived gate, not an arbitrary one — compliant. 3 lineage — mixed: fqx_* is FMP quarterly (dated), bs_ebit_turned is base_snapshot (undated), fmp_dyn_* is the dynamics overlay (quarter-dated). 4 coverage — global, no SEC-only leg. 5 NaN direction — see issue 1, the recency NaN-passes is the wrong direction for a data-validity-flavored guard. 6 units — none, ratio/flag based. 7 definitions — seven flags, four sources, four different "turn" definitions collapsed into one OR (already flagged in audit-3, still true). 8 code correctness — no forward reference or sign bug found. 9 regression — 422->302, intended per the recency fix; not over-tightened, matches the source's window. 10 tiers — 6 exceptional, 1 elite (the only elite-bearing archetype found so far in this slice) out of 302; on 8 lenses. 11 overlap — 100% subset of fallen_deep_value, see header. 12 new layers — see above.

### arch_mb_fallen_stressed
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_LATENT_CLUSTERS.md "overlevered_stressed + fallen_angel" (3.09x/2.67x) and the triple conjunction with deep_value (3.2x/3.7x); master_archetype_reference VII Akre AMT ("debt panic + visible FCF inflection"), Wolf Archetype 8 "Cash-flow deleveraging" / Archetype 10's "reject if too far gone"; the compendium's post-reorg lens (diagnose the type of distress). The thesis is stress that eventually RESOLVES, priced as an equity call option on survival.
- As coded (l.7464): `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _mb_stressed`, where `_mb_stressed` (l.7487-7489) is now a FOUR-branch OR: `(nde in [5,90)) | (equity<0) | (fq_equity<0) | (net_cash_pct_mcap<=-1.0) | (debt_to_equity>=2.0)` — the last two are the audit-3 addition (a second stress path for EBITDA<=0 names, whom the `nde` 99-sentinel excludes). Lenses (10, dump3): dist_hi260(-), ev_sales(-), fqx_ebit_ttm_g(+), cfo_yield(+), mcap(-), 13D(+), and four audit-3 resolution lenses: fq_netdebt_decline_months(+), fq_interest_cover(+), fmp_st_financing_outflow_years(+), fmp_altman_z(+). 937 firers (verified), 18 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 ranked suggestion #1 ("add a second stress path for EBITDA<=0 names") landed exactly as proposed (`net_cash_pct_mcap<=-1.0 | debt_to_equity>=2.0`) and is the entire explanation for the count moving 606 (audit-3) -> 937 now (+55%): the population the `nde=99` sentinel used to exclude (the MOST stressed, EBITDA-negative names) is now admitted via the balance-sheet-leverage branch. This is a verified, intended widening, not a bug — it is exactly the "not a no-op" fix audit-3 asked for, and the resulting members are genuinely stressed by an independent measure (net cash worse than -100% of cap, or D/E>=2), not an artefact. Suggestion #3 (Altman as a soft veto/lens) landed as a LENS (`fmp_altman_z`, +1) — correctly NOT a gate, per the USER RULE, since "reject if irreparable" is Wolf's qualitative reject rule, not a source-stated number.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `equity<0` (same-currency balance sheet) still treats a buyback-driven negative book (a franchise that has bought back more than its retained earnings, not a distressed one) as "stressed" — audit-3 flagged this and it is unchanged; with the new D/E>=2 branch also present, a healthy-cash-flow, negative-book franchise can now ALSO qualify via `equity<0` alone even if `debt_to_equity` and `net_cash_pct_mcap` both look fine, since the branches are OR'd, not required together.
  2. The four "resolution" lenses are unweighted equally with the eight-lens set as a MEAN (per the `_spirit` mechanism at l.9960-9990), so a name resolving on ONE of the four (say `fq_interest_cover` alone) scores the same as a name resolving on all four; there is no way to read from the flag alone whether the "equity option on survival" thesis's resolution path is actually underway for a given member versus merely not-yet-tested.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5` (fg_*, global) or `fg_bvps_up_share5` as a "the balance sheet has been rebuilding for years, not just this quarter" corroboration, sharper than the single `fq_netdebt_decline_months` lens; no evh_* application (multiple-history is not this archetype's axis).
- Suggestions:
  1.   2. [spirit] Add `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5` as a resolution-lens corroboration alongside `fq_netdebt_decline_months`.

- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_LIFT2.md §5 Intersections: fallen_insider_conviction AND smart_money_wreckage (n=1,739, lift 5.76x vs 3.92x/4.69x, blow-up 31%). master_archetype_reference III "insider buying clusters at sentiment troughs" crossed with Wolf Archetype 10 distressed/deep value. This is a real fix, not cosmetic: `arch_mb_fallen_insider` guarantees `_ins_2q==True`, which alone makes `_smart_legs>=1`, and the OLD `smart_money_wreckage`-only test (`_smart_legs>=1`) was therefore trivially satisfied by every fallen_insider member — the exact algebraic collapse audit-3 identified (`conviction_confluence == fallen_insider & _mb_deep`). ### arch_mb_asset_trough_informed
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_SEGMENTS.md "Asset-based businesses" GMM cluster 3 (2.2x, activist 38%, insiders 12%, weeks since 5y low=1) and the winners-vs-lookalikes table (gap_sales_1y +0.06, the ONLY conviction separator): an asset business at a fresh low whose sales-per-share have run ahead of the price, with an informed buyer arriving; deleveraging was NEGATIVE in the mined table. master_archetype_reference I-E "The Surviving Thing" + Wolf Archetype 6 (commodity producers) + III (insider clusters at troughs).
- As coded (l.8410): `_mb_base & _seg_asset & _mb_fallen & _nl_sales_lead & _informed_g`. `_seg_asset` (l.8392-8395) = Energy/Materials/Real Estate/Utilities sector OR an industry-string regex (shipping/mining/oil/steel/etc.), AND NOT a drug developer. `_nl_sales_lead = _crank(max(nl_sales_1y,nl_sales_2y,nl_sales_3y).where(_seg_asset)) >= 0.60` (l.8407-8408) — the audit-3 fix, a within-asset-segment RANK replacing the old bare `>0` test. `_informed_g = _informed | _corp_conviction | _inst_arrival` (l.8409), where `_informed = _ins_2q | _13d_recent | _mb_insider` — the audit-3 fix adding the non-SEC `_corp_conviction` path. 23 firers (verified), 52% US by domicile, 1 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: BOTH of audit-3's core suggestions landed. Suggestion #2 ("rank `nl_sales_1y` within `_seg_asset` instead of `>0`, per the study's top-feature framing") landed as described, using the MAX of the 1y/2y/3y lag lenses rather than just 1y — a reasonable, slightly broader reading of "sales ahead of price" than literally proposed, and it is now a genuine top-40%-of-asset-segment rank, not a near-automatic sign test. Suggestion #1 ("add a non-SEC path to `_informed`") landed PARTIALLY: `_corp_conviction` (global buyback/share-shrink) is a real non-SEC leg, but `_inst_arrival` (US 13F) is not, so the informed leg is now "SEC OR global-corporate-conviction OR US-13F", not fully global. This explains the count jump 6 (audit-3) -> 23 now (+283%): the widened informed leg plus the rank-based sales-lead leg together materially broadened the population, and the US share DROPPED from audit-3's reported 100% to 52% (domicile) — a real, verified widening of reach, consistent with the intended fix. Suggestion #3 (fresh-low as a leg/exceptional-tier promotion) and suggestion #4 (filter 13D/A, or require a %-of-class increase) did NOT land: `_13d_recent` (l.1867) is unchanged (`evt_sc13d_date` age<=365 & mcap<2e9), still admitting 13D/A amendments (including sell-downs) as "arriving", and still carrying the hidden mcap<2e9 cap on the activist path only.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `_13d_recent`'s hidden `mcap<2e9` cap (unrelated to the archetype's own liquidity/size lenses) means a $3bn asset-trough name with a fresh 13D cannot use the 13D path at all, only the insider-quarters or corp-conviction paths — this silently shapes which SIZE of name can qualify via which INFORMED sub-path, without appearing anywhere in the archetype's own gates or lenses.
  2. `_seg_asset`'s industry regex (`shipping|marine|tanker|lessor|leasing|holding|reit|...`) still catches non-shipping "holding" companies (conglomerates) as audit-3 noted; unfixed, low-impact given the archetype's small size (23 firers).
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_rev_ps_3y_cagr`/`fg_rev_ps_5y_cagr` (fg_*, global) could corroborate `_nl_sales_lead` with a dated, multi-year per-share sales trend rather than the (partly Yahoo-snapshot-derived) narrative-lag construction; no clean esb_*/evh_* application (this archetype's facts are asset-cheapness and informed-buying, not earnings surprises or multiple history).
- Suggestions:
  1. [data] Add the N-PORT global holder-`change`>0 leg to `_informed_g` (still the single biggest remaining reach gap, per audit-3 suggestion #1 and the parallel gap in conviction_confluence).
  2. [method] Filter 13D/A amendments out of `_13d_recent` (or require `percentOfClass` to have increased) so "arriving" cannot mean "reducing"; this affects every archetype that reads `_13d_recent` (asset_trough_informed, fallen_deep_value's lens, smart_money_wreckage, conviction_confluence), so fixing it once at the shared helper fixes it everywhere.
  3. [method] Drop or raise the `mcap<2e9` cap inside `_13d_recent` so it does not silently exclude larger names from the 13D path specifically while leaving them eligible via the other `_informed_g` branches.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — sales-ahead-of-price now a genuine rank; leverage-as-lever is present only as a lens (`debt_to_equity`, +1), correctly not gated (not a source-stated number). 2 gates — `_mb_fallen<=0.40`, `_crank>=0.60` are close readings of the mined cluster's own framing; the hidden `mcap<2e9` inside `_13d_recent` (issue 1) is an UNDOCUMENTED, arbitrary size cap riding along inside a shared helper — flag: this is exactly the kind of non-thesis gate the USER RULE asks to demote, but it is buried in a helper used by many archetypes, not written as this archetype's own gate, so it evades the audit unless traced through `_informed_g` -> `_informed` -> `_13d_recent`. 3 lineage — `_seg_asset` from industry/sector strings (global); `_nl_sales_lead` from engine narrative-lag construction (fq_rev_growth/fmp_st_sales_ps growth vs ts_r*, global, mixed dated/snapshot); `_informed_g`'s components are SEC (usf_*, EDGAR), US 13F, or global (corp_conviction). 4 coverage — meaningfully improved (52% US now vs audit-3's 100%) but still SEC/US-13F-weighted for 2 of the 3 `_informed_g` branches. 5 NaN — `.fillna(False)` throughout, correct. 6 units — none (ranks/flags). 7 definitions — none found beyond issue 1's buried cap. 8 code correctness — none found. 9 regression — 6->23, verified intended widening from the two landed fixes. 10 tiers — 1 exceptional/23 (4%), 0 elite, 12 lenses. 11 overlap — independent of the fallen_deep_value family (different sector population, `_seg_asset`-gated); not a dedup candidate. 12 new layers — see above.

### arch_mb_biotech_financed_hiring
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_SEGMENTS.md "Drug developers" cluster 3 (3.65x, blow-up 35%; AXSM, EXEL, CORT, ITCI): headcount growing in every member, share count +15%, insiders 36%, activist 59%, price 22% of the 5y high, cash on hand; the 10x patterns add `downgrades_12m HIGH` as a positive. master_archetype_reference I-F "The Optional Thing" (the option mispriced as dead; the balance sheet survives to the catalyst).
- As coded (l.8439): `is_operating & (mcap>=10e6) & _is_drug_dev & (ts_dist_hi260<=0.50) & _bio_financed & _bio_committed & _bio_runway`. `_bio_financed = (fmp_st_shares_growth_3y>=0.10) | (fq_financing_cf>0)` (unchanged). `_bio_runway` (l.8434-8436, the audit-3 fix): `(cash/(4*trailing-quarter-burn) >= 1.0yr) | (fq_cfo>=0) | (runway is NaN & net_cash_pct_mcap>0.10)` — a genuine cash-vs-burn calculation replacing the old bare sign test. `_bio_committed` (l.8437-8438, the audit-3 fix): `(usf_emp_g1>=0.10) | _informed_g | (usf_emp_g1.isna() & fmp_rd_to_revenue>0 & fq_rev_growth>=0.10)` — a genuine GLOBAL branch added beside the SEC headcount test. 31 firers (verified), 29% US by domicile, 2 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 suggestion #2 ("replace `net_cash_pct_mcap>0` with a runway measure from `fq_cash_sti` and trailing `fq_cfo`") landed exactly, and correctly retains the OLD net-cash sign test only as a last-resort fallback for names where the runway calc itself is NaN (a defensible, narrowed use of the weaker test). Suggestion #3 ("give `_bio_committed` a global branch") landed, using R&D-disclosed-and-growing plus revenue growth as the global proxy for "commitment" instead of the SEC-only headcount test — a reasonable substitute, though it measures INVESTMENT commitment, not the study's literal headcount-growth fact, for the global branch specifically. Suggestion #1 ("gate on `_mb_base` like every sibling") did NOT land: the core is still `is_operating & mcap>=10e6` with no `ts_dvol26_usd` liquidity floor — confirmed unchanged at l.8440, the only other mb_ archetype besides `grew_into_valuation_turning` missing this floor. Suggestion #4 (promote `sent_downgrades_12m` to the exceptional tier) did NOT land — it remains a lens only (per the general tier mechanism, which the USER RULE would in any case keep it as, since no source states a threshold for it — so leaving it a lens is actually the RIGHT call under the new rule, even though it diverges from the literal audit-3 ask).
- Methodology issues:
  1. No liquidity gate (see above) — an illiquid OTC clinical-stage biotech can pass every other leg and fire; every sibling mb_ archetype (except grew_into_valuation_turning) requires `ts_dvol26_usd>=250_000` via `_mb_base`.
  2. `_bio_runway`'s primary branch divides `fq_cash_sti` by `4 * trailing-quarter-burn` — a single quarter's burn annualized, which can be noisy for a name with one unusually low- or high-burn quarter (e.g., a one-off financing-related cash outflow inflating the "burn" and understating runway, or a quiet quarter before a trial ramp understating true forward burn).
  3. `_bio_committed`'s global branch requires `fq_rev_growth>=0.10` — for a PRE-REVENUE clinical-stage developer (a core part of this archetype's population, given `_is_drug_dev` includes clinical names), `fq_rev_growth` is likely NaN or undefined, so the ENTIRE global branch is unusable for the population most in need of a non-SEC "committed" signal; the branch effectively only helps a revenue-generating (more commercial-stage) drug developer.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_rd_g1`/`fg_shares_dil_g1` (fg_*, global, 30.9k names) as a direct, global "committed" signal (R&D spend growing, share count growing — the literal per-share dilution+R&D-investment fact the study measured) replacing or corroborating the revenue-growth-gated branch in issue 3, since `fg_*` does not require positive revenue to compute a per-share R&D or share-count growth trend.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Gate the core on `_mb_base` (or at minimum `ts_dvol26_usd>=250_000`) to match every other mb_ sibling; audit-3's suggestion #1, still open.
  2. [data] Replace `_bio_committed`'s global branch's `fq_rev_growth>=0.10` condition with `fg_shares_dil_g1>=0.10` or `fg_rd_g1>0` (fg_*, revenue-independent), so pre-revenue clinical names — the population this branch exists to reach — can actually use it.
  3. [method] Use a TTM or 2-quarter-average burn rate in `_bio_runway`'s denominator rather than a single trailing quarter, reducing the noise flagged in issue 2.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — financed+committed+runway now genuinely measured (2 of 3 legs materially improved from audit-3); headcount-growth-in-every-member (the study's strongest claim) is only one OR-branch of `_bio_committed`, not required. 2 gates — `>=0.10` share growth, `<=0.50` price, `1.0yr` runway are reasonable readings of "financed"/"22% of the high"/"cash on hand" but the exact thresholds are not literally in the source (the source states levels like "22% of 5y high" as a MEDIAN, not a cutoff) — flag: `ts_dist_hi260<=0.50` is looser than the study's median and is acknowledged already in audit-3 as "fine as a population boundary", but strictly it is the engine's own choice, not a source number; low-priority flag given its role as a population boundary rather than a selective gate. 3 lineage — `_is_drug_dev` from industry/sector/name strings (global); `fq_financing_cf`/`fq_cfo`/`fq_cash_sti` from FMP quarterly (dated); `usf_emp_g1` SEC-only; `fmp_rd_to_revenue` global. 4 coverage — no liquidity floor (issue 1); `_bio_committed`'s global branch is revenue-gated (issue 3), so effectively narrower than "global" implies. 5 NaN — `_bio_runway`'s NaN-fallback direction is a defensible cascade (runway NaN -> check CFO -> check net-cash sign), not a silent pass; correct. 6 units — cash/burn in reporting currency, consistent per name; no cross-currency issue found. 7 definitions — none new found beyond issue 3. 8 code correctness — none found. 9 regression — 3->31 (+933%), verified as the intended combined effect of the runway and global-committed fixes, not a bug — though the liquidity-gate omission (issue 1) does let illiquid names through: verified via pandas, 8 of 31 firers (26%) have `ts_dvol26_usd` below the $250k floor or missing entirely, i.e. would fail `_mb_base` if it were applied. 10 tiers — 2 exceptional/31 (6%), 0 elite, 10 lenses. 11 overlap — independent population (`_is_drug_dev`-gated, distinct from `_seg_asset` and from the fallen-deep-value family) — not a dedup candidate. 12 new layers — see above (fg_* fixes the revenue-gating problem in issue 3).

### arch_mb_inflecting_operator
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_LATENT_CLUSTERS.md cluster 0 (38% of 2018+ multibaggers, 1.1x): margins and EBIT rising, returns improving, smaller cap, a fair (not bubble) price; FORENSICS §5 adds that winners had a WEAKER tape than lookalikes. archetype_compendium Part I-8 / Part II-B Andreola; master_archetype_reference I-A(15).
- As coded (l.7499): `_mb_base & (mcap<2e9) & _mb_margin_up & _mb_ebit_up & _mb_roic_up & (_eveb in (0,25])`. `_mb_margin_up = (op_margin_delta_yoy>=0.01) | (fqx_inc_ebit_margin_dt>=0.20)` (l.7531, audit-3 fixed the second branch to the domain-limited column). `_mb_ebit_up = (fqx_ebit_ttm_g>=0.10) | (fqx_ebit_ttm_g.isna() & ebit_growth_yoy>=0.10)`. `_mb_roic_up = (fqx_roic_ttm>roic_lindy) | (roce_delta_yoy>0)`. 1,141 firers (verified), 30 exceptional, 1 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 ranked suggestion #1 ("use `fqx_inc_ebit_margin_dt` (domain-limited), consistent with the engine's own drop-through rule") landed exactly — the raw `fqx_inc_ebit_margin` (which audit-3 showed could read 374% from a loss base and still pass "margin up") is gone from this test; only the `_dt`-suffixed, domain-limited version (values >1.0 excluded as "losses unwinding" per l.1176) remains. This adequately explains most of the count move 1,379 (audit-3) -> 1,141 now (-17%). Suggestion #2 ("add the perception half as lenses: `evt_react_last`(-), `ts_r13`(-), `sent_n_analysts`(-)") landed — all three, plus `rel_ind_ev_ebit`(-), are in the current dump3 lens list and were not in audit-3's. Suggestions #3 ("require the safe branches when data exist") and #4 ("frame the price leg relatively") did NOT land: the three ORs each still have one weak branch (`op_margin_delta_yoy>=0.01`, one point of margin; `ebit_growth_yoy>=0.10` from a possibly-negative base via yartseva pct_change; `roce_delta_yoy>0`, any improvement) that can each independently satisfy its leg, and `(_eveb in (0,25])` is still an absolute EV/EBIT cap with no peer-relative alternative in the core (only `rel_ind_ev_ebit` as a lens).
- Methodology issues:
  1. The conjunction can still be satisfied ENTIRELY by the three weak branches simultaneously (a 1pp margin improvement, a 10% EBIT print from a small negative base via the sign-ambiguous yoy branch, and a token +0.1pp ROCE delta) with none of the three "strong" (dated, magnitude-real) branches ever firing — audit-3's issue (e) is unchanged.
  2. `roic_lindy` is a multi-year MEDIAN (per edgar_roic_roiic.py, confirmed in the mb_b peer review of a sibling archetype using the same helper); `fqx_roic_ttm>roic_lindy` therefore means "above average", not "at its own high" as the cluster's "returns improving" framing might suggest — a low bar, unchanged from audit-3.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr>0` or `fg_ocf_ps_3y_cagr>0` (fg_*, global, 30.9k reach) as a per-share, multi-year corroboration that would require the STRONG branches' magnitude rather than the weak branches' token improvements — a natural gate-tightening candidate for the "returns improving" fact if promoted to a lens (or, per the USER RULE, kept a lens and blended at 25% via `_DEMOTED` rather than gated, since no source states a specific fg_* threshold). `evh_ev_ebit_log_chg_1y` (evh_*, ~1,000 names today) as a future replacement for the absolute `(_eveb<=25)` cap with an own-history-relative read, once coverage grows.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Where `fqx_ebit_ttm_g` is populated (i.e., not relying on the sign-ambiguous fallback), require it over the weaker `ebit_growth_yoy` branch; and require `fqx_roic_streak>=2` alongside `roce_delta_yoy>0` so "improving" cannot be a single-quarter token tick.
  2. [spirit] Add `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr` (fg_*, global) as a lens (not a gate, since no source number exists for it) corroborating "returns improving" with a dated multi-year per-share trend.
  3. [method] Keep `(_eveb<=25)` as the sanity-band gate (defensible as an EV-sanity guard under the USER RULE) but add `rel_ind_ev_ebit<=0.60` as an ADDITIONAL lens (already present) — no core change needed here since the absolute cap is closer to a data-validity band than an invented quality floor, given 25x is a generous ceiling, not a tight quality cut.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — margin+EBIT+ROIC rising, smaller cap, fair price all present; "weaker tape" now a lens (landed), "fair not bubble" still an absolute EV/EBIT cap rather than a peer-relative measure. 2 gates — `mcap<2e9` and `(_eveb<=25)` are population-boundary-style absolute levels tied to the study's own framing (small-cap, non-bubble); defensible as thesis-adjacent, not obviously arbitrary — no clear USER RULE violation found here, unlike the buried `mcap<2e9` inside `_13d_recent` flagged under asset_trough_informed (which is a different, undocumented instance of the same NUMBER). 3 lineage — `op_margin_delta_yoy`/`ebit_growth_yoy`/`roce_delta_yoy`/`_eveb` from asymmetry_global (EDGAR/Yahoo TTM, snapshot); `fqx_*` from FMP quarterly (dated); `roic_lindy` EDGAR median filled by `fmp_st_roic_lindy` (global). 4 coverage — global, no SEC-only leg in the core. 5 NaN — `.fillna(False)` throughout, correct. 6 units — pp deltas and ratios, no currency issue. 7 definitions — see issue 1 (three ORs, each mixing a strong dated branch with a weak snapshot/token branch under one gate). 8 code correctness — none found. 9 regression — 1,379->1,141, verified intended per the landed `_dt` fix. 10 tiers — 30 exceptional/1,141 (2.6%) and 1 elite — the highest exceptional RATE and the only other elite besides fallen_value_turn in this slice, on a moderate 10-lens list. 11 overlap — independent of the fallen-deep-value family (no `_mb_fallen` requirement at all; in fact many members may be NEAR their highs, the opposite population) — not a dedup candidate. 12 new layers — see above.

### arch_mb_grew_into_valuation_turning
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_ARCHETYPES.md Archetype B (grew into the valuation: revenue +13%, margin at the 64th pct of own history) with the profit turn arrived. archetype_compendium Part I-3 Gardner Rule Breaker Sub-B "Already re-rated: the multiple compressed 50%+ through earnings growth, not price decline" (NVDA 131x->40x, SE, CRWD, MELI, NU).
- As coded (l.7549): `(arch_derate_through_growth==1) & (_margin_trend_up | _mb_turn) & (fq_rev_growth>=0.08)`. `arch_derate_through_growth` is defined upstream (l.~6820-6850) with its own population `is_operating & mcap>=10e6` — NO `ts_dvol26_usd` liquidity requirement. `_margin_trend_up = (fqx_opm_slope8>0 & fqx_opm_consist>=0.6) | (fqx_margin_inflect_now==1)`. `_mb_turn` now carries the global recency fix (`<=12 months or NaN`, l.7483). 1,792 firers (verified against archetype_tags.csv), 15% US, 37 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 ranked suggestion #1 ("gate on `_mb_base` like every sibling") did NOT land: confirmed by direct code inspection (no `_mb_base` or `ts_dvol26_usd` anywhere in this assignment or in `arch_derate_through_growth`'s own gate) AND by data — verified via pandas that 421 of the 1,792 firers (23.5%) have `ts_dvol26_usd` below the $250,000 floor or missing entirely, i.e. would fail `_mb_base` outright if it were applied, exactly like every other mb_ sibling requires. Suggestion #3 ("drop `_mb_turn` from the OR, or keep it only with `fqx_m_since_turn_positive<=12`") landed PARTIALLY, via the shared `_mb_turn` redefinition (the same fix that also affects fallen_value_turn) rather than a change local to this archetype — and carries the same caveat noted under fallen_value_turn: the recency AND is bypassed (`| isna()`) for any of `_mb_turn`'s seven OR-branches whose underlying source does not populate `fqx_m_since_turn_positive`. Suggestion #2 ("add a `multiple now fair` leg or lens") landed as LENSES only (`fmp_dyn_ev_sales_change_3y`(-), `ev_ebit.where(>0)`(-), `fqx_m_since_turn_positive`(-)) — correctly not gated, since Sub-B's "already re-rated" is not the archetype's own stated number, so a lens is the USER-RULE-compliant placement. The count move 2,480 (audit-3) -> 1,792 now (-28%) is explained mainly by the `_mb_turn` recency tightening (issue shared with fallen_value_turn), NOT by the (unlanded) liquidity gate.
- Methodology issues:
  1. This is the SECOND mb_ archetype (with biotech_financed_hiring) still missing the `_mb_base` liquidity floor every other sibling in this slice requires; here the effect is quantified and large (23.5% of firers illiquid or unmeasured), on the slice's SECOND-LARGEST archetype by firer count (1,792), so any book or ranking built from this flag is materially diluted by untradeable names.
  2. `_margin_trend_up | _mb_turn`: the margin-TREND branch (8-quarter slope + consistency, or a dated inflection) is a much stronger signal than `_mb_turn`'s any-historical-sign-flip OR (even with the recency fix, a name whose flip source has no date bypasses the 12-month window entirely, per issue shared with fallen_value_turn) — the two are still mixed under one OR with very different evidentiary weight, unchanged from audit-3's finding.
- Where the new layers apply: `fg_rev_ps_3y_cagr`/`fg_eq_ps_5y_cagr` (fg_*, global, 30.9k reach) as a fully-dated, multi-year corroboration of "grew into the valuation" (Archetype B's own framing is multi-year, not the single-quarter `fq_rev_growth>=0.08` gate); `evh_evs_vs_med_3y` (evh_*, ~1,000 names today, grow into a lens as coverage widens) as the direct "multiple now fair" test Sub-B describes, sharper than the `fmp_dyn_ev_sales_change_3y` lens already present.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Gate on `_mb_base` (or at minimum `ts_dvol26_usd>=250_000`), matching every sibling; this is the single highest-value, still-open fix in the slice given the archetype's size (1,792 firers, 23.5% illiquid).
  2. [method] Require the recency test unconditionally on every `_mb_turn` OR-branch (the same fix proposed under fallen_value_turn — fixing the shared `_mb_turn` helper once resolves it for both archetypes).
  3. [spirit] Add `fg_rev_ps_3y_cagr` as a lens corroborating the "grew into the valuation" multi-year framing, since `fq_rev_growth` alone is a single-period read.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — de-rating-through-growth plus a turn signal are present, but the "already re-rated" (multiple now fair) is a lens, not a ceiling, so a name that de-rated from 60x to 35x still qualifies (audit-3's original spirit-gap, unchanged). 2 gates — `fq_rev_growth>=0.08` is close to but below Archetype B's own median (13%); a defensible thesis-derived floor, not obviously arbitrary. The missing `_mb_base` gate is not a "gate that should be removed" under the USER RULE — it is a gate EVERY sibling correctly has and THIS archetype is missing, the opposite kind of flag from what the USER RULE targets, but worth stating precisely since the brief's rule is about gates that are present and shouldn't be, not gates that are absent and should be added; I flag it as a methodology/spirit gap, not a USER-RULE violation. 3 lineage — `arch_derate_through_growth`'s own multiple-compression math (l.6823-6845) now reads `evh_*` first with an `fmp_dyn_ev_sales_change_3y`/annualized-CAGR fallback (per the header's shared note on evh_* reach); `_margin_trend_up`/`_mb_turn` are FMP-quarterly-dated with base_snapshot/dynamics-overlay branches. 4 coverage — global, no SEC-only leg; the missing liquidity gate is the coverage/quality issue here, not a data-reach one. 5 NaN — `.fillna(False)` on the whole core; `_mb_turn`'s internal recency NaN-passes (issue 2) is the one flagged direction problem. 6 units — none, ratios/flags. 7 definitions — see issue 2 (heterogeneous OR). 8 code correctness — none found beyond the shared `_mb_turn` issue. 9 regression — 2,480->1,792, correctly attributed above to the recency fix rather than the (absent) liquidity fix. 10 tiers — 37 exceptional/1,792 (2.1%), 0 elite, 9 lenses. 11 overlap — depends entirely on `arch_derate_through_growth` (a non-mb_ archetype, out of slice scope) as its base population; not a dedup candidate within this slice. 12 new layers — see above.

### arch_mb_compounder_insiders_at_high
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_OPERATORS.md "Near highs" 10x patterns (lift 90-108x on tiny support; NVDA 2015/2019, MSTR 2020, TSLA 2019, ABMD 2013, ETSY 2017): within 15% of the 52w high, ROCE in the industry's top quartile, R&D-heavy, insiders buying, recent quarters NOT beating. archetype_compendium Part I-1 Meyer Phelps 100x (sustained ROIC, founder alignment); master_archetype_reference VI Andreola (buy at 52w highs with low institutional ownership).
- As coded (l.7694): `_mb_base & (ts_dist_hi52>=0.85) & (rel_ind_roce>=0.75) & _rd_heavy & (_ins_2q | _mb_insider | _corp_conviction)`. `_rd_heavy = (fmp_rd_to_revenue>=0.08) | (fmp_rd_intensive_flag==1)`. 44 firers (verified), 61% US, 1 exceptional, 0 elite.

### arch_mb_hiring_beating_uncovered
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_OPERATORS.md "Uncovered" k-means, the only lifted cluster (2.1x, blow-up 15%; 2930.T, BEL.NS, HARVIA.HE, TRIDENT.NS, TATAELXSI): headcount +36%, margins at the top of own history, beats and surprises, EV/sales already rising, new 13F holders, 56% of the 5y high, NO analyst. archetype_compendium Part II-B Andreola footprint (discovery cycle: buy before retail/institutional coverage).
- As coded (l.7706): `_mb_base & _hiring & (_mb_opm_gap>=0.02) & _beating & (sent_n_analysts<=1) & ts_dist_hi260.between(0.35,0.80)`. `_hiring = (usf_emp_g1>=0.15) | (usf_emp_g1.isna() & fq_rev_growth>=0.20)`. `_beating = (evt_beat_share_8q>=0.6) | (evt_surprise_4q>=0.05) | (fmp_earnings_beat_rate>=0.6)` — the `>=0.05` materiality floor is the audit-3 fix. `sent_n_analysts<=1` has NO `.fillna(0)` any more (the audit-3 fix; NaN now fails via `.fillna(False)` on the whole comparison). 20 firers (verified), 5% US, 0 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: BOTH audit-3 core suggestions landed as specified — suggestion #3 (materiality floor on the surprise branch) and suggestion #1 (observed-count semantics: NaN is unknown, not zero). Together these explain the LARGE count move 65 (audit-3) -> 20 now (-69%). Verified via pandas (direct query on `archetype_tags.csv` merged with `fmp_sentiment.csv`): ALL 20 current firers have `sent_n_analysts` EXACTLY 1.0 — none is 0, none relies on a NaN-as-zero read. This CONFIRMS the fix landed correctly in direction, but it also reveals the fix's cost: `_beating` requires an EPS ESTIMATE to exist (a "beat" needs a consensus), so this archetype's population NOW REQUIRES a grades-feed row with a nonzero analyst count for BOTH legs to cohere — meaning a name with LITERALLY ZERO coverage (no analyst has ever rated it, hence no row in `fmp_sentiment.csv` at all, hence `sent_n_analysts` is NaN, not 0) can never pass `sent_n_analysts<=1` under the new (correct) NaN-fails semantics, even though that name is the study's own paradigm case (2930.T, BEL.NS etc. are described as having "no analyst"). The fix correctly eliminated a false-positive population (names with genuinely unknown coverage wrongly read as "0 analysts") but appears to have also eliminated the true positive population the study describes, leaving only the narrow "exactly 1 analyst on file" slice — this is a genuine, data-verified spirit tension, not a simple win.
- Methodology issues:
  1. See regression check: the archetype's population is now provably "exactly one analyst reported, and that analyst's estimate was beaten" — a real but narrower reading of "uncovered" than the study's "no analyst" cases. This is worth surfacing explicitly rather than leaving implicit in the flag's name.
  2. `_hiring`'s fallback (`fq_rev_growth>=0.20` when `usf_emp_g1` is NaN) still substitutes a DIFFERENT fact (revenue growth) for headcount growth for the entire non-US population (since `usf_emp_g1` is SEC-only) — unchanged from audit-3, unfixed; audit-3's suggestion #2 (store `profile.fullTimeEmployees` globally) did not land.
- Where the new layers apply: `esb_*` (17,513-name reach, 8,755 non-US) is EXACTLY the fix for issue 1's core tension: `esb_beats_8q`/`esb_surprise_4q` are populated for many names that have NO row in `fmp_sentiment.csv`'s grades feed at all (a beat/surprise record does not require an active sell-side RATING, only an EPS estimate on file, which the bulk earnings-surprises feed carries independently) — so a genuinely obscure, low-coverage name can show a real beat record via `esb_*` even where `sent_n_analysts` is NaN. Propose reading "uncovered" as `sent_n_analysts.fillna(0)<=1` ONLY when corroborated by an actual `esb_*` beat record existing (i.e., `esb_beats_8q.notna()`), so a name with a genuine earnings history but no sentiment/grades row is not excluded, while a name with NEITHER any grades row NOR any earnings-surprise history (true total obscurity, likely untracked entirely) is still excluded for lack of any measurable "beating" fact.
- Suggestions:
  1. [data] Corroborate/widen `_beating` using `esb_beats_8q`/`esb_surprise_4q` (which reach 8,755 non-US names `evt_*` alone does not) and pair it with `sent_n_analysts.isna() | sent_n_analysts<=1` (treat "no sentiment row but a real esb_* earnings record exists" as a legitimate uncovered-but-tracked case), closing the gap this review found between the correctly-fixed NaN semantics and the narrowed population it produced.
  2. [data] Pursue audit-3's still-open suggestion #2 (store `profile.fullTimeEmployees` over time) so `_hiring` gets a genuine global headcount branch instead of the revenue-growth substitute.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — headcount, margin-gap, beating, uncovered, tape-band all present; "new 13F holders" absent from core (US-only lens elsewhere in the file, not here). 2 gates — `>=0.15`/`>=0.20`/`>=0.02`/`<=1`/`0.35-0.80` are all close readings of the study's own cluster statistics; compliant. 3 lineage — `usf_emp_g1` SEC-only (dated); `evt_*` now esb_*-filled (global, per the file-level merge at l.286-292, dated); `sent_n_analysts` grades-historical (12,440-name reach, snapshot). 4 coverage — bounded tightly by the sentiment overlay's reach for the "uncovered" leg specifically (issue 1) — this is the slice's clearest case of a coverage-overlay's OWN reach limit inverting the archetype's intended population. 5 NaN — now correct (fails) on `sent_n_analysts`, per the landed fix; correctly conservative. 6 units — pp deltas / ratios, no currency issue. 7 definitions — none new found beyond issue 1/2. 8 code correctness — none found; the landed fix is logically sound, its EFFECT is the finding. 9 regression — 65->20 (-69%), data-verified and explained precisely (not a mystery collapse) — the biggest proportional move of any archetype in this slice. 10 tiers — 0 exceptional, 0 elite on 20 members — consistent with such a small, homogeneous population (all `sent_n_analysts==1`) compressing the lens-rank spread. 11 overlap — independent population, no dedup concern. 12 new layers — see above (esb_* is the direct fix).

### arch_mb_cheap_growth_targets_up
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_OPERATORS.md "Not fallen" k-means cluster 7 (39% of not-fallen multibaggers, 1.25x, blow-up 8%; ISCTR, ALARK, STRL, 6920.T, PGSUS, TRIL.NS): revenue +17%, EV/EBIT 8.5, FCF yield+growth the top axis, targets revised up, 70% of the 5y high. master_archetype_reference II Yartseva (FCF/P dominant) + Lynch PEG/GARP; the compendium's Andreola "room to expand: <20x EBITDA".

Suggestion #3 ("require `fcf_yield.notna()` in the FCF branch explicitly") landed too — the current code reads `fcf_yield.notna() & (...)`, whereas audit-3's dump showed a plain sum that silently fell through to NaN (and hence to the EV/EBIT branch) without the explicit guard; now explicit. Suggestion #2 (a global revision series from successive `analyst-estimates` snapshots) did NOT land — `_pt_up`'s two branches (`sent_pt_rev_q`, `evt_pt_rev_90d`) remain US/CA-centric (2,896 and 2,547-name reach respectively per audit-3's coverage note), so the archetype is STILL 78% US-domiciled despite the cluster's own members being dominated by Turkish, Indian and Japanese names (ISCTR, ALARK, 6920.T, TRIL.NS) — the reach gap audit-3 identified is entirely unaddressed.
- Methodology issues:
  1. The reach gap (issue above) is now, if anything, MORE visible: with the chase-veto removing many US-momentum false positives, the surviving 107 are disproportionately the population the "targets revised up" leg CAN see (US/CA), while the cluster's actual geographic center (Turkey/India/Japan) remains structurally invisible to `_pt_up` for want of a global revision series.

- Suggestions:

  2. [method] Consider requiring `_eveb` and `fcf_yield` to at least be READ on a comparable footing (e.g., report which branch fired, similar to the `mb_deep_branch` suggestion elsewhere), so "cheap for growth" is auditable per member.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — revenue growth, cheapness, target-revision-not-chasing, tape-band all present; geographic mismatch with the source cluster remains the dominant spirit gap. 2 gates — `>=0.15`, `<=10`, `>=0.20`, `>=0.60` are the study's own cluster statistics; compliant, and the chase-veto is itself now correctly a GATE since "rising ahead of price, not chasing it" is literally the thesis's own qualifier, not an arbitrary addition. 3 lineage — `sent_pt_rev_q` FMP sentiment (US/CA-weighted, snapshot); `evt_pt_rev_90d`/`evt_pt_chase_flag` price-target-news (US/CA, dated); `fcf_yield`/`_eveb` asymmetry_global (snapshot). 4 coverage — the slice's clearest surviving US/CA-only reach gap on an explicitly GLOBAL source cluster; unresolved. 5 NaN — `fcf_yield.notna()` explicit guard now present (fixed); `_pt_up`'s NaN handling is conservative (both branches fail on NaN, so no coverage-gap-as-pass issue here, just a coverage-gap-as-silence issue). 6 units — none, ratios. 7 definitions — see issue 2 (two unreconciled cheapness axes). 8 code correctness — none found. 9 regression — 191->107 (-44%), correctly and fully attributed to the landed chase-veto fix. 10 tiers — 2 exceptional/107 (2%), 0 elite, 10 lenses. 11 overlap — independent population (not-fallen, near 70% of high) from the fallen family; no dedup concern. 12 new layers — n/a in practice (see above); the real fix needs a data pull, not a blend of the three existing new layers.

### arch_mb_industry_trough_cheapest
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_UNCOVERED.md "Uncovered, all" 3x candidates (U1): fallen, P/S bottom quintile, the industry's median margin change OR growth in the bottom quintile; robust 5.2-5.8x, 110-175 events, 8-12 markets (SARDAEN, VEDL, 300274.SZ, BTE.TO/YGR.TO, ADANIENT 2013). archetype_compendium Part II-D Capital Cycle ("the turn occurs at maximum pessimism as the weakest competitor throws in the towel"). master_archetype_reference I-E(9) Regime-change cyclical.
- As coded (l.7756): `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _q_lo(_psv) & _ind_trough`, where `_ind_trough = _q_lo_ind(ind_tape_opm_d1) | _q_lo_ind(ind_tape_rev_growth)` (l.7776-7782). `_q_lo_ind` (defined l.7776-7781) ranks the industry-level MEDIAN itself among peer GROUPS (one observation per `_peer_key`, via a `groupby(level=0).first()` collapse) rather than among names, then maps the cut back — the audit-3 fix. 260 firers (verified), 28% US, 10 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 ranked suggestion #1/#6 ("rank industry variables among industries... so the bottom quintile is not a function of industry size") landed EXACTLY as specified, using the same `_q_lo_ind` helper now shared with `fallen_operator_industry_low`. This explains the count move 306 (audit-3) -> 260 now (-15%): a large, low-margin industry can no longer fill the entire bottom-quintile cut simply by having many names; the cut is now made once per peer group. Suggestion #2 ("add a survivor leg, `fq_interest_cover>=1.5` or `fmp_altman_z>=1.8`") did NOT land: the current dump3 lens list (`p_s`(-), `ind_tape_opm_d1`(-), `ind_tape_rev_growth`(-), `ts_dist_hi260`(-), `nl_sales_3y`(+), `ts_ma30_slope13`(-), `mcap`(-)) has no survival-style lens at all — a real, verified gap, especially notable since the SAME survivor-lens idea WAS added to `fallen_deep_value`, `fallen_stressed`, `fallen_below_cycle`, and `fallen_trough` in this same audit-3 pass; this archetype (and its sibling `fallen_operator_industry_low`) were left out of that treatment. Suggestion #3 (S3 small-market fallback) is the shared `_crank`/`_q_lo`/`_q_hi` mechanism, already global to the file and unrelated to this archetype specifically.
- Methodology issues:
  1. Survivor-lens inconsistency (see above): four sibling trough/fallen archetypes in this exact commit family received a "not too far gone" lens; this one and `fallen_operator_industry_low` did not, despite both explicitly invoking the same capital-cycle "weakest competitor" framing that MOTIVATES a survivor check (the compendium's own words are "the weakest competitor throws in the towel" — i.e., some do NOT survive, and the archetype should distinguish the survivor from the one that dies).
  2. `_q_lo(_psv)` (cross-sector, within-market P/S bottom quintile) still means commodity/contracting industries dominate the P/S leg (as audit-3 noted); this is the study's own finding (SARDAEN, VEDL) so not a bug, just worth restating as a population-shape fact.
  3. The `_ind_trough` OR (margin-change-low OR growth-low) can be satisfied by a "growth low, margin EXPANDING" industry, which is a mixed signal the archetype cannot distinguish from a genuinely-troughed one — unchanged from audit-3, unfixed.
- Where the new layers apply: none of esb_*/fg_*/evh_* bear directly on an INDUSTRY-level (not per-name) fact; the survivor leg (issue 1) is better served by the already-on-file `fq_interest_cover`/`fmp_altman_z` (used successfully elsewhere in this exact audit-3 pass) than by any of the three new layers.
- Suggestions:
  1. [spirit] Add the SAME survivor lens used on `fallen_deep_value`/`fallen_stressed` (`fq_interest_cover`(+), `fmp_altman_z`(+)) here and on `fallen_operator_industry_low`, for consistency within one audit pass and because both archetypes' own sources explicitly invoke "the weakest competitor" dying.
  2. [method] Consider requiring the margin-change branch and the growth branch of `_ind_trough` to agree in SIGN direction (both non-expanding) rather than accepting either alone, closing methodology issue 3.
- Checklist: 1 fidelity — fallen + cheap-on-sales + industry-trough all present; survivor test entirely absent (issue 1), unlike four siblings. 2 gates — `_q_lo`/`_q_hi` quintiles are the study's own convention; compliant. 3 lineage — `p_s` asymmetry_global (snapshot); `ind_tape_opm_d1`/`ind_tape_rev_growth` engine peer-group medians of dated (FMP quarterly) and snapshot (Yahoo fallback) sources. 4 coverage — global, no SEC-only leg. 5 NaN — each industry variable's OR branch fails independently on NaN (`.fillna(False)`), correct. 6 units — pp deltas / ratios, no currency issue. 7 definitions — see issue 3 (mixed margin/growth trough signal). 8 code correctness — none found; the `_q_lo_ind` fix is correctly implemented and shared cleanly with its sibling. 9 regression — 306->260, verified intended, matches the landed fix precisely. 10 tiers — 10 exceptional/260 (3.8%), 0 elite, 7 lenses. 11 overlap — shares `_mb_fallen` with the broader family but its industry-trough fact is independent of the deep-value/turn/accel facts; not a dedup candidate. 12 new layers — n/a (see above); the missing survivor lens is the priority fix, using EXISTING columns, not the new layers.

### arch_mb_growth_past_capex_peak
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_UNCOVERED.md "Uncovered, not fallen" 3x candidates (U4): two-year revenue growth top quintile (or capex/D&A high), no payout, capex rolling off while still above D&A, ROIC at its own high or volatile vs industry; robust 7.1-7.5x, 80-104 events, 9-12 markets (TSLA 2018, FNOX.ST, 001570.KS, IIVI, HTHT). archetype_compendium Part II-D Capital Cycle at company level ("falling capex/depreciation ratios" as the investment phase ends); master_archetype_reference VII Akre AMT.
- As coded (l.7781): `_mb_base & (ts_dist_hi260>=0.60) & (_q_hi(_g2) | _q_hi(fq_capex_to_da)) & _no_payout & _capex_rolloff & (_roic_own_hi | (_crank(ts_vol_1y)>=0.8))`. `_g2 = fmp_st_revenue_3y_cagr.where(notna, fmp_st_revenue_cagr)` (l.7815, a fixed-3y CAGR preferred over the old variable-span CAGR-or-1y-fallback). `_capex_rolloff = (|fq_capex|<|fq_capex_p|) & (fq_capex_to_da>1.0)` (unchanged, still single-quarter). `_no_payout = ~((dividend_yield>0.005)|(buyback_yield>0.005)).fillna(False)`. 100 firers (verified), 6% US, 1 exceptional, 1 elite.
- Regression check: a PARTIAL, unheralded fix landed here beyond what audit-3's dump described: `_g2` is now `fmp_st_revenue_3y_cagr` (a FIXED 3-year span) preferred over `fmp_st_revenue_cagr` (the old variable-span, up-to-8-year CAGR), rather than audit-3's described `fmp_st_revenue_cagr.fillna(fq_rev_growth)` (which mixed a multi-year CAGR with a ONE-year growth rate under one quantile). This is a real improvement — the two statistics now both span multiple years (3y primary, variable-span fallback), closing the WORST part of audit-3 methodology issue (a) (a 1-year growth rate no longer silently enters the same quantile as a multi-year CAGR). However, audit-3's other three suggestions did NOT land: suggestion #1 (build `_capex_rolloff` on TTM vs prior-TTM from the quarterly panel) — still a single quarter vs its prior-period value (`fq_capex` vs `fq_capex_p`), confirmed unchanged; suggestion #2 (FCF inflection as a leg/lens) — not in the dump3 lens list (`fmp_st_revenue_3y_cagr`(+), `fq_capex_to_da`(+), `fqx_fcfm_slope8`(+), `fq_capex_p.abs()-fq_capex.abs()`(+), `fqx_roic_ttm-roic_lindy`(+), `ts_vol_1y`(+), `dividend_yield`(-)) — wait, `fqx_fcfm_slope8` IS present as a lens now, so suggestion #2 DID land as a lens (correcting my initial read); suggestion #3 (`owner-earnings` growthCapex/maintenanceCapex split) is not yet a catalogued FMP endpoint pulled into the engine, unconfirmed/still open; suggestion #4 (explicit NaN handling on `_no_payout`) did NOT land — same silent-NaN-passes pattern verified earlier (a name with no dividend/buyback data at all still reads "no payout"). The count move 92 (audit-3) -> 100 now (+9%) is modest and, given NO core-tightening fix landed (the `_g2` change is a definitional cleanup, not obviously tightening or loosening in a predictable direction) is most plausibly ordinary data-refresh drift rather than an attributable code change — flagged as unverified precisely, stated as the most likely explanation.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `_capex_rolloff` still compares ONE quarter against its immediately preceding quarter (not TTM vs prior-TTM), so a seasonal capex pattern (common in capital-intensive builders) can trip the "roll-off" leg on ordinary quarterly lumpiness rather than a genuine multi-quarter capex peak having passed.
  2. `_no_payout` still silently passes a name with no dividend/buyback data as "not paying" (verified via the NaN-comparison semantics established under fallen_ignored_believers) — the same still-open issue.
- Where the new layers apply: `owner-earnings`'s growthCapex/maintenanceCapex split (A2 §A.1, still not catalogued/pulled per this review) remains the correct fix for separating a genuine "growth capex rolling off" from "maintenance capex cut" — no new layer among esb_*/fg_*/evh_* substitutes for it directly, but `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5` (fg_*, global) is a reasonable proxy corroboration that cash compounding is real once capex eases, usable as a lens now.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Rebuild `_capex_rolloff` on TTM-capex vs prior-TTM-capex from the cached quarterly panel (both quantities are already computable from `fq_capex` accumulated over four quarters), removing the single-quarter seasonality noise.
  2. [method] Make `_no_payout`'s missing-data direction explicit (`dividend_yield.notna() | buyback_yield.notna()` required before the veto can apply, or read `.fillna(True)` on the underlying flags to make "unknown payout" fail rather than silently pass as clean).
  3. [data] Pursue the still-open `owner-earnings` growthCapex/maintenanceCapex pull (A2 §A.1) as the definitive fix for the growth-vs-maintenance-capex ambiguity.

### arch_mb_divergence_cheapest_pb

Together these explain the count move 218 (audit-3) -> 191 now (-12%): a modest, correctly-directed tightening (removing software/negative-book names whose "cheapest P/B in the industry" was a leverage/goodwill artefact rather than genuine asset mismarking, and removing shrinking-but-high-margin names from the margin branch). Suggestion #2 ("add pb-vs-own-history as a lens from `fmp_dyn_*`/market-cap history") did NOT land — no such lens is in the current dump3 list (`narrative_lag_extent`(+), `rel_ind_pb`(-), `ts_vol_1y`(+), `ind_tape_rev_growth`(-), `ts_dist_hi260`(-), `nl_fcfps_3y`(+)); this is now directly addressable with `evh_*` (see below), which did not exist at audit-3 time.

The `_asset_like` population restriction audit-3 suggested (suggestion #1's alternative form, "restrict to `_asset_like` | tangible-asset intensity>=0.3") did NOT land — the archetype still applies "cheapest P/B in the industry" to every operating industry, including asset-LIGHT ones, relying on `pb<=1.5` alone (issue 1) to do the sanity-guarding work that a population restriction would do more precisely.

[method] Consider restricting the P/B leg's population to `asset_intensity_ppe>=0.3` (or `_asset_like`, already defined elsewhere in the file) as a companion to `pb<=1.5`, so "cheapest P/B" more precisely means "cheap assets" per Kerrisdale's framing rather than relying on the absolute cap alone.

## Slice summary: the ten most valuable findings/augmentations (ranked)

1. [method, count hygiene] `arch_mb_fallen_value_turn` (302) and `arch_mb_fallen_value_accel` (118) are literal, pandas-verified 100% algebraic subsets of `arch_mb_fallen_deep_value` (854) — each simply ANDs one more fact onto the same core. Neither is in `_DEDUP_CLUSTERS` (l.9401), so `archetype_count` over-credits one underlying fact (fallen + deep value) by up to 3x; 73% of fallen_deep_value's own members also fire >=1 of {value_turn, value_accel, fallen_stressed, fallen_insider, fallen_trough}, averaging 2.11 of these 6 columns lit per member. Add value_turn/value_accel to a dedup cluster with fallen_deep_value; leave stressed/insider/trough out (verified NOT literal subsets — each adds an independent third fact).
2. [method, USER RULE-adjacent] Two archetypes still lack the `_mb_base` liquidity floor every other mb_ sibling requires: `grew_into_valuation_turning` (1,792 firers — verified 421, 23.5%, would fail `ts_dvol26_usd>=250k`) and `biotech_financed_hiring` (31 firers — verified 8, 26%, would fail). The first is the slice's second-largest archetype by count; fixing it is the single highest-leverage remaining change.
3. [method] `compounder_insiders_at_high`'s insider leg `(_ins_2q | _mb_insider | _corp_conviction)` still contains the audit-3-identified redundant bypass: because `_mb_insider` includes the bare `insider_buy_flag==1` (a single Form-4 purchase) unconditionally, the whole expression algebraically reduces to `usf>=2 | insider_buy_flag==1 | distinct>=2 | net_usd>0 | _corp_conviction` — a single purchase satisfies the leg even when `usf_ins_buy_quarters_4q` is populated and shows fewer than 2 buying quarters. This is now live on 44 members (was 13 at audit-3), a larger population riding on the same unfixed logic. Fix: use `usf` alone when populated; fall back to `_mb_insider`'s distinct-buyer/net-USD test (not the bare flag) only when `usf` is NaN.
4. [data, verified] `hiring_beating_uncovered` correctly fixed its NaN semantics (missing coverage now fails, not passes) but the fix is data-verified to have narrowed "uncovered" to EXACTLY "1 analyst on file, and that analyst's estimate was beaten" — all 20 current firers have `sent_n_analysts==1.0` precisely, none via the old NaN-as-zero path. A genuinely zero-coverage name (the study's own paradigm case: 2930.T, BEL.NS) has no grades row at all and is now excluded outright. Fix: corroborate coverage-status with `esb_beats_8q.notna()` (17,513-name reach, including obscure names with no active sell-side rating but a real earnings-surprise record), so "no sentiment row but a real esb_* record" still qualifies.
5. [spirit, consistency] Four fallen/trough archetypes (`fallen_deep_value`, `fallen_stressed`, `fallen_below_cycle`, `fallen_trough`) received a "not too far gone" survivor lens (`fq_interest_cover`, `fmp_altman_z`) in the audit-3 pass; two siblings that explicitly invoke survival in their OWN source text — `industry_trough_cheapest` ("the weakest competitor throws in the towel") and `fallen_operator_industry_low` ("find the highest-torque SURVIVOR") — did not. Add the same two lenses to both for consistency within one audit pass.
6. [data] `evh_*` (dated EV/sales and EV/EBIT history) is now genuinely wired into the merge (l.296) and already feeds `arch_derate_through_growth`'s core (hence `grew_into_valuation_turning`), but `fmp_ev_history.csv` holds only ~1,000 of 46,526 names today (built after this review began) — every evh_* suggestion in this report (fallen_deep_value, fallen_below_cycle, divergence_cheapest_pb, improving_unturned_sellside, inflecting_operator) should be wired as a LENS only, weighted by coverage, until the file's reach grows; do not gate on it yet anywhere in this slice.
7. [data] `esb_*` (universe-wide earnings-surprise history, 17,513 names / 8,755 non-US) already fills `evt_*` on ingest (l.286-292) and therefore already broadens `hiring_beating_uncovered`'s `_beating` leg and `fallen_value_turn`'s `evt_react_last`/`evt_ignored_beats_2y` lenses for free; the one place it should be read DIRECTLY (not via the evt_ fill) is finding #4 above, where the coverage-status question, not the beat-record question, is what's missing.
8. [method] `fg_*` (per-share compounding history, 30,932 names) is unused anywhere in this slice's core or lenses despite being fully wired and broadly reached; the highest-value adds are: `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5`/`fg_rev_ps_5y_min5` as through-cycle quality lenses on the whole fallen family (replacing single-quarter/TTM snapshots); `fg_shares_dil_g1`/`fg_rd_g1` as `biotech_financed_hiring`'s global `_bio_committed` branch (fixing that branch's current `fq_rev_growth>=0.10` gate, which is UNUSABLE for pre-revenue clinical names — the exact population the global branch exists to reach); `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr` as `compounder_insiders_at_high`'s still-missing Phelps-test compounding leg.
9. [method] Missing-data direction: THREE archetypes (`fallen_ignored_believers`, `growth_past_capex_peak`, `improving_unturned_sellside`) share one unfixed pattern — a negated dividend/payout veto (`~(dividend_yield>0.02)` or equivalent) silently passes a name with NO dividend data at all as "clean", verified via direct NaN-comparison semantics (`NaN>0.02` evaluates False, so the negation is True). One shared helper fix (`dividend_yield.notna() & (...)`) closes all three at once.

  3. `market` in `mb_model_scores.csv` (the model's own within-month-market rank key, `mb_model_rank_mkt`) is the model's fit-time exchange grouping; the engine's `country` (`src`) used for `mb_model_rank_base` is a different key. This is the intended, audit-3-directed fix (re-rank within the engine's own liquid-base population) but it means "top decile" here is measured on a different population/grouping than either the model's own backtest OR MULTIBAGGER_MODEL.md's §1 walk-forward numbers — the 2.6x/3.1x figures quoted in the spirit paragraph are not this population's own number.

- Checklist (12-point): 1 spirit legs present (rule membership AND model top-decile); no thesis leg is missing, but see methodology #1 for a spirit MISMATCH (fallen bias). 2 `>= 0.90` and `>= 1` are literally the study's own top-decile and "any rule" definitions (thesis numbers) — no arbitrary gate found. 3 `mb_model_scores.csv`, weekly-scored, staleness-guarded at 42 days; `mb_rule_count` is same-panel, same-week. 4 global (the model scores 35,308 names across all markets); no US-only leg in this archetype itself (its 33 rule inputs individually vary). 5 `.fillna(False)` on the model-rank comparison correctly fails a stale/missing score. 6 no currency issue (the model's features are pre-normalized; not re-derived here). 7 one statistic (`mb_model_rank_base`) at one cut (0.90). 8 no forward reference (verified above); no dead branches. 9 881 firers matches dumps3/CSV/live recompute exactly — no regression. 10 4 lenses/881 members, 87 exceptional (9.9%), 5 elite (0.6%) — a normally-populated tier, unlike most of this slice's narrower boxes. 11 by definition overlaps every rule archetype it counts; `archetype_count` will double- or triple-count intersection members (methodology #2) — a [data] count-hygiene item. 12 see above (esb_* only; fg_*/evh_* not needed).
- Suggestions:
  1. [spirit] Split the lens/label by rule-family: confluence built on a NOT-fallen rule (compounder_insiders_at_high, cheap_growth_targets_up, rd_leader_on_volume, growth_past_capex_peak, lean_rd_stocking_up, leader_in_wave) is where MODEL.md's own numbers say the lift is real (2.6-3.1x); confluence built only on fallen rules is where the model "adds least" (1.5x) per the same source. Carry this as a `mb_confluence_family` flag or as two archetypes rather than one blended tier.
  2. [method] Drop the `(ts_dist_hi260, -1)` lens or replace it with `(ts_dist_hi260, +1)` given finding #1 — as coded it rewards exactly the population the source says the model helps least.
  3. [method] Weight `mb_rule_count` by DISTINCT parent situations rather than raw column count, or cap it at the number of non-intersection rule families a member belongs to, so an intersection member is not mechanically scored as "more confluent."
  4. [data] Note in the book/label that "top decile" here is the engine's own liquid-base ranking, not the walk-forward backtest's population, so the quoted 2.6x/3.1x MODEL.md figures describe a related but not identical population.
