### arch_mb_model_region_rule
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_MODEL.md §3, "The top-decile region as a tree" (depth-4 tree over month x market ranks; best leaf: `op_vs_mkt_disthi <= 0.12 & mcap_usd_log <= 0.13 & vol52 > 0.72` — leaf 5, lift 3.901, blow-up 37.7%; second-best leaf: `op_vs_mkt_disthi <= 0.12 & mcap_usd_log > 0.13 & vol52 > ... & dd_time_share_260 > 0.73` — leaf 6, lift 3.117, blow-up 29.6%). "A readable, lottery-shaped rule the boxes did not have."
- As coded now (line 8470-8473, added in 50f8dac after the audit-3 report was written — this archetype has no audit-3 section of its own): `_mb_base & _crank(vs_mkt_dist_hi260) <= 0.12 & _crank(ts_vol_1y) >= 0.72 & (_crank(mcap) <= 0.13 | _crank(ts_dd_time_share_260) >= 0.73)`. Lenses (6): vs_mkt_dist_hi260 -, ts_vol_1y +, market_cap_usd -, ts_dd_time_share_260 +, mb_model_p +, ts_wks_since_lo260 -. 647 firers, count not yet in an audit-3 dump but matches CSV/live recompute exactly.
- Regression check: n/a — this archetype postdates audit-3 (added in 50f8dac, the same commit that fixed the sign bugs elsewhere), so there is no prior audit-3 finding to regress against. I verified it independently instead (see "as coded" and methodology).
- Verified against source: I read MULTIBAGGER_MODEL.md §3 directly (lines 139-186). The tree's actual split values are `op_vs_mkt_disthi <= 0.12`, `mcap_usd_log <= 0.13`, `vol52 <= 0.72` (i.e. the "True"/multibagger branch is `vol52 > 0.72`), and, on the other branch, `dd_time_share_260 <= 0.73` vs `> 0.73`. The engine's four cuts (0.12 / 0.72 / 0.13 / 0.73) are an EXACT, literal match to the tree's own printed split points, and the two leaves are combined with OR exactly as the tree's own two "class: True" leaves are structured (small-cap OR long-in-drawdown, both gated on the same `disthi<=0.12` and `vol52>0.72` stems). This is the cleanest USER RULE compliance case in the slice: every threshold is a number the source states, verbatim.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `vs_mkt_dist_hi260` (the engine's `op_vs_mkt_disthi`) is computed as own `ts_dist_hi260` minus the COUNTRY's median `ts_dist_hi260` (`mkt_tape_dist_hi260`, line 7638-7643) — the source's tree was fit on ranks "within month x market" where "market" is the model's own exchange key, not the engine's `src` country field. As with the other two model archetypes, this is a population/grouping mismatch inherited from the same root cause, not a new bug.
  2. Unlike model_top/confluence/uncovered_not_fallen, this archetype's `mb_model_p` lens is the ONLY tie back to the model's probability — the CORE itself never reads `mb_model_p`, only the four tree features. That is faithful to the source (the tree is a description of the region, not a probability cut) but means this archetype can fire for a name the model does NOT currently score highly (e.g. a stale/missing `mb_model_p` after the 42-day cutoff) — worth stating explicitly since the other two "model" archetypes gate on the score itself.
  3. No staleness or blow-up lens: leaf 5's own blow-up is 37.7% (the highest blow-up quoted anywhere in MULTIBAGGER_MODEL.md for this family) and leaf 6's is 29.6%, yet neither `fmp_altman_z` nor any survivability lens is present (model_top added exactly this pair of lenses for its own high-variance tail; this archetype, with a stated blow-up nearly as high, did not get the same treatment).
- Where the three new layers apply: `fg_shares_dil_g_max3` and `evh_evs_log_chg_1y` as independent readings of "how far gone" a leaf-5/6 member is (a small-cap, high-vol, deep-drawdown name whose multiple has ALSO compressed hard is a purer match to the tree's shape than one where only the price legs qualify); `fmp_altman_z` (+) as the missing blow-up lens, matching model_top's own treatment.
- Checklist (12-point): 1 spirit faithful; every core threshold IS the source's own tree split (see "verified against source" above) — no missing thesis leg. 2 clean: all four thresholds are literal source numbers; no arbitrary gate. 3 `vs_mkt_dist_hi260`/`ts_vol_1y`/`ts_dd_time_share_260` all from ts_snapshot (global, weekly); `market_cap_usd` global; `mb_model_p` only in the lens, weekly-scored with the shared 42-day staleness guard applied upstream. 4 global archetype, no SEC-only leg. 5 `.fillna(False)` throughout; correct direction (NaN cannot claim a rank extreme). 6 no currency issue (ranks, not levels). 7 one statistic per leg, matching the tree exactly (no mixed TTM/FY or min/median ambiguity). 8 no forward reference (confirmed: `arch_mb_model_region_rule` is assigned after `mb_rule_count` is computed, so it correctly excludes itself from that count too, same as its two siblings). 9 no audit-3 baseline (archetype is new since the last audit); 647 firers today, consistent between CSV and live recompute. 10 6 lenses/647 members; count not given in the dump for exceptional/elite tiers but the archetype was not present in the audit-3 report to compare against — worth the next reviewer confirming exceptional/elite counts land sensibly given how narrow the four-way AND is. 11 shares the market-vs-country grouping mismatch with model_top/confluence/uncovered_not_fallen (methodology #1) — a common-cause item across all four "model" archetypes, worth fixing once, not four times. 12 see above.
- Suggestions:
  1. [spirit] Add `fmp_altman_z` (+) as a blow-up lens, matching the treatment model_top already received — this archetype's own stated blow-up (30-38%) is at least as high.
  2. [data] Note in the comment that the core does not itself require a fresh/high `mb_model_p` (only the four tree features), so a name can be a region_rule member with a stale or low model score; if that is not intended, add `mb_model_p.notna()` as an explicit data-validity condition.
  3. [method] Once the market-vs-country grouping question is resolved for model_top/confluence (suggestion there), apply the same resolution here for consistency, since all four model archetypes share the same `_crank`/country machinery.

### arch_mb_fallen_less_than_industry_financed  (engine name; slice file's old name was `arch_mb_neglected_fell_more_financed`)
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_UNCOVERED.md's U5 family, "Uncovered, fallen — 10x within 5 years": robust 7.0x, 49 events, 9 years, 11 markets, blow-up 29%, 10x rate 7% (ROCK-A.CO 2015 33x, TTRAK.IS 2019, GULFNAV.AE 2022, EUZ.DE 2017, 3324.TWO 2014). The mined condition, per audit-3's forensic read of the mining code (`multibagger_uncovered.WORDS/FRAME`, ranked WITHOUT a sign flip), is "distance from 5y high MINUS the industry's high, HIGH": the name is deeply fallen in absolute terms but has held up BETTER than its own industry — plus financing dependence (share issuance funding an FCF burn), book value compounding, and neglect (<=1 analyst).
- As coded now (line 7820-7833): `_mb_base & _mb_fallen` (own `ts_dist_hi260<=0.40`) & `_financed` (`fmp_st_shares_growth_3y>=0.05 & fcf_yield<0`, OR `fq_financing_cf>0`) & `_book_growing` (`_q_hi` of `equity_cagr_5y.fillna(fmp_st_equity_cagr)`) & `_q_hi(vs_ind_dist_hi260)` & `sent_n_analysts.fillna(0)<=1`. Lenses (6): vs_ind_dist_hi260 -1, equity_cagr_5y +1, fmp_st_shares_growth_3y +1, sent_n_analysts -1, ts_dist_hi260 -1, ts_dd_time_share_260 +1. Comment (line 7820-7822) now correctly describes the mined condition in words ("held up BETTER than its industry"). 0 firers (verified three ways: `archetype_tags.csv` sum, a fresh live engine recompute, and the engine's OWN sanity report, which prints "ZERO arch_mb_fallen_less_than_industry_financed fires on NOBODY — investigate" on every run); 0 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check of the audit-3 fix: THE SIGN FIX ITSELF LANDED (commit 50f8dac changed `_q_lo(df['vs_ind_dist_hi260'])` to `_q_hi(df['vs_ind_dist_hi260'])` and renamed both the archetype and its comment), but the fix as landed CATASTROPHICALLY OVER-TIGHTENED — the archetype now fires on literally nobody, which is the worst possible form of "firer count collapse" the brief asks me to check for. I traced the cause with a live recompute (audit4/full_inner_df.pkl): among the 1,916 `_mb_base & _mb_fallen & _financed` names, `vs_ind_dist_hi260` (own `ts_dist_hi260` minus the industry's median `ts_dist_hi260`) has max = 0.2157 and median = -0.2216 (n=1,876 non-NaN). The base-wide top-quintile cut (`_q_hi`, i.e. `_crank >= 0.80`) that `vs_ind_dist_hi260` must clear sits at roughly +0.22 or higher across the WHOLE `_mb_base` population (75th percentile of the whole base is already 0.2167). Algebraically: to be `_mb_fallen` (own `dist_hi260<=0.40`) AND in the base-wide top quintile of `vs_ind_dist_hi260` (own minus industry median `>= ~0.22`), the industry's median `dist_hi260` must sit at `<= 0.40 - 0.22 = 0.18` or lower — i.e. the TYPICAL name in the peer group must itself be down about 82% from its own 5-year high. That joint condition (a fallen name in an industry whose median member is even MORE devastated, while ALSO being a share-issuing, book-compounding, uncovered name) essentially never occurs in the current cross-section. The audit-3 sign correction was right about the DIRECTION but the fix note never checked whether the resulting AND-of-five was still satisfiable — it was not. A second, independent bug in the same fix: the LENS (line 9825) still reads `(_c('vs_ind_dist_hi260'), -1)` — it was never flipped when the gate was, so even if the gate is repaired to admit members, this lens would rank them backward (rewarding names that fell MORE than their industry, the opposite of the now-corrected gate).
- Methodology issues:
  1. [confirmed, see above] The archetype is currently completely non-functional (0 members) — this is not a subtle methodology nit, it is the headline finding for this box.
  2. `_q_hi(vs_ind_dist_hi260)` is ranked against the WHOLE `_mb_base` (all liquid operating names), not within the `_mb_fallen` sub-population the archetype actually draws from. Every other "which fifth of THIS population" leg in the file that needed a conditioned rank (e.g. `peer_worst_cheapest`'s new `_operator_early` gate, or `_q_lo_ind`'s per-industry-group cut) demonstrates the engine already has the pattern for a population-conditioned rank; this leg does not use it.
  3. `_financed`'s two branches measure different things at different frequencies: `fmp_st_shares_growth_3y>=0.05 & fcf_yield<0` is a 3-year FY-basis issuance test paired with a snapshot FCF yield, while `fq_financing_cf>0` is a single TTM quarterly cash-flow-statement line that also picks up DEBT raised (not just equity) — a name that raised debt with positive FCF passes this branch even though the study's "financing dependence" was specifically an equity-issuance-funding-a-burn condition (per audit-3's read).
  4. `sent_n_analysts.fillna(0)<=1`: within `_mb_base`, 41.7% of names have no analyst count on file at all (verified, full_inner_df.pkl) — "neglected" here is still substantially "not covered by the sentiment feed," not necessarily "few analysts follow it and are unenthusiastic," per the still-open A2 §top-9 finding.
- Where the three new layers apply: `evh_evs_vs_med_3y` or `evh_ev_mcap_ratio` would give an EV-sanity-checked read on whether a "financed" name's issuance is diluting its own multiple, corroborating `_financed`; `fg_shares_dil_g1`/`fg_shares_dil_g_max3` (global, per-share, annual) is a cleaner, FY-consistent issuance measure than the `fmp_st_shares_growth_3y` + `fq_financing_cf` mismatch in methodology #3; `fg_eq_ps_5y`/`fg_bvps_up_share5` (per-share, 5-year, consistency-checked) is a better version of `_book_growing` than the current `equity_cagr_5y.fillna(fmp_st_equity_cagr)` mix (aggregate equity CAGR vs per-share book value CAGR are two different quantities, an unresolved audit-3 finding that also did not land).
- Checklist (12-point): 1 the financing/book-growth/neglect thesis legs are present, though `_financed` and `_book_growing` each mix two different underlying quantities (methodology #3, and the equity_cagr_5y/fmp_st_equity_cagr aggregate-vs-per-share mismatch audit-3 already flagged and which is unchanged). 2 `>=0.05` (share growth), `<0` (fcf_yield), and the two quintile cuts are engine-native operationalizations of source states, not literally stated numbers, but they mirror the study's own quintile-based mining method, so I read them as faithful implementations rather than USER RULE violations; the ND=5 style "hard state cutoff" concern does not apply here. 3 `fmp_st_shares_growth_3y`/`fmp_st_equity_cagr` from fmp_statements (global, FY); `fq_financing_cf`/`equity_cagr_5y` from fmp_quarterly/EDGAR (equity_cagr_5y itself is EDGAR-only, ~10% coverage per the audit-3 doc's shared facts, filled by the FMP twin); `sent_n_analysts` 27% coverage. 4 global archetype in principle (no SEC-only leg), but see #4 above on analyst-coverage as a false "neglected" signal, and note the population is currently EMPTY so there is no live US/non-US split to report. 5 verified: NaN in `equity_cagr_5y` correctly falls through to `fmp_st_equity_cagr` before ranking (fillna, not an isna-passes trap); ### arch_mb_preprofit_freefall_informed
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_SEGMENTS.md, "Pre-profit operators — k-means Archetype 2" (10% of that population's multibaggers, lift 1.49x, blow-up 28%; GME 2019, ASPN 2018, EAT 2020, BGFV, LSCC, CAR 2019): fallen_angel 88%, price 18% of the 5y high, P/S 0.30; states over-represented `productivity_gain` 34% (8.8x), `insider_buying` 30% (5.8x), `new_activist` 45% (5.1x), `fund_price_divergence` 46%, `deep_value` 64%.
- As coded now (line 8397-8410, 8426): `_seg_preprofit` (`op_margin<0 | fcf_margin<0`, not a drug developer, not asset-like) & `_mb_base` & `_mb_fallen` (own `dist_hi260<=0.40`) & `_informed_g` (`_informed` [`_ins_2q | _13d_recent | _mb_insider`] OR `_corp_conviction` [buyback executed or share count shrinking now] OR `_inst_arrival` [`fmp_inst_new_q0>=1`]). Lenses (9): ts_dist_hi260 -1, ts_wks_since_lo260 -1, usf_ins_buy_quarters_4q +1, -evt_sc13d_date_age +1, usf_emp_g1 -1, p_s -1, evt_pt_prem_12m +1, nl_sales_1y +1, market_cap_usd -1. 666 firers, 24 exceptional, 0 elite (matches dumps3/CSV/live recompute).
- Regression check: LANDED and materially broadened reach, verified. Audit-3's central complaint was that `_informed` was SEC-only in practice (insider quarters, SC 13D, EDGAR Form 4 — all US), so a global cluster study could never fire on a non-US member. The dd7fb41 fix widened `_informed` to `_informed_g` by OR-ing in two new global-reaching legs (`_corp_conviction`, `_inst_arrival`). I verified with a live recompute that this is doing real, non-trivial work: of the 666 current members, only 16.8% qualify via the strict SEC insider-quarters leg, while 68.5% qualify via `_inst_arrival` and 50% via `_corp_conviction` — 29.0% of members satisfy `_informed_g` via `_corp_conviction` ALONE (neither the SEC insider leg nor `_inst_arrival` also true for them). This is a genuine broadening, not a no-op fix.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `fmp_inst_new_q0` (13F "new positions this quarter") is itself a US-listed-securities feed (13F filers report positions in US-listed instruments, including ADRs) — so `_inst_arrival`'s reach, while broader than the pure insider/13D legs, is still not a genuinely non-US-listed signal; a name listed only on, say, the Tokyo or Warsaw exchange with no ADR still cannot qualify through this leg. Audit-3's specific ask (an N-PORT-based non-US arrival signal) did not land — this remains an open gap for non-ADR non-US pre-profit names, just a narrower one than before the fix.
  2. `_corp_conviction`'s two branches (`fmp_st_buyback_yield_y0>0.01` or `fqx_share_shrink_now==1`) are COMPANY actions, not "an informed buyer arriving" in the sense the study's `insider_buying`/`new_activist` states meant — a pre-profit, cash-burning name buying back stock is a genuinely unusual signal worth having, but labelling it under the same `_informed_g` umbrella as insider/13D/institutional arrival conflates two different mechanisms (a board's capital-allocation choice vs an outside party's revealed conviction).
  3. `_seg_preprofit` uses `fcf_margin<0` ALONE (via the OR with `op_margin<0`) as suficient for "pre-profit" — a profitable, GAAP-positive operator having one heavy-capex year with negative FCF margin qualifies as "pre-profit," which the study's own label (an operator segment defined by a k-means state, not a single ratio) would likely not have grouped there. Unresolved from audit-3.
  4. `_13d_recent` (feeding into `_informed`) counts SC 13D/A AMENDMENTS, which include an existing holder's EXIT filing, not only a new arrival — so a holder selling down can register as "informed conviction arriving." Unresolved from audit-3.
- Where the three new layers apply: `esb_react_last`/`esb_pead_4w` would let a market-reaction-based "someone is paying attention" signal stand in for, or corroborate, the company-action-only `_corp_conviction` branch for non-US names that `fmp_inst_new_q0` cannot reach; `fg_shares_dil_g1<0` is a cleaner, FY-consistent version of "share count shrinking now" than `fqx_share_shrink_now` for names without a full quarterly panel.
- Checklist (12-point): 1 the fallen/deep/informed-arrival thesis legs are present; `productivity_gain` (headcount shrinking while revenue holds, 8.8x, the cluster's single strongest state) is only approximated by a bare `usf_emp_g1 -1` lens with no revenue-per-employee pairing (unresolved from audit-3). 2 no arbitrary non-thesis gate found; `_informed_g`'s thresholds (`>=2` quarters, `>0.01` buyback yield, `>=1` new position) are each either the study's own state definition or a >0/nonzero data-validity-style bar, not an invented quality floor. 3 usf_*/evt_sc13d_date are US/SEC-only (7,021 / 3,309 names per the shared audit-3 coverage facts); `fmp_st_buyback_yield_y0`/`fqx_share_shrink_now`/`fmp_inst_new_q0` are the newer global-reaching legs (with the 13F caveat in methodology #1). 4 69.5% of members have `usf_ins_buy_quarters_4q` data present (a rough US-filer proxy, verified) — the archetype is now meaningfully less US-concentrated than before dd7fb41, though not fully global (methodology #1). 5 `.fillna(False)` throughout the informed-buyer OR; correct direction. 6 no currency issue (ratios/flags). 7 `_seg_preprofit`'s `op_margin<0 | fcf_margin<0` mixes two different profitability definitions under one OR (methodology #3). 8 no forward references found. 9 666 firers, matches dumps3/CSV/live recompute exactly — no collapse; the informed-buyer widening changed COMPOSITION (verified above) without a count regression. 10 9 lenses/666 members, 24 exceptional (3.6%), 0 elite. 11 shares `_mb_fallen` and informed-buyer legs conceptually with `smart_money_wreckage`/`asset_trough_informed`; no explicit cross-reference in the book. 12 see above.
- Suggestions:
  1. [data] Add an N-PORT-based (`funds/disclosure-holders-latest`, global fund holdings) new-holder signal to `_informed_g` for names `fmp_inst_new_q0` cannot reach (non-ADR, non-US-listed).
  2. [spirit] Build the `productivity_gain` state properly: `usf_emp_g1<0 & fq_rev_growth>usf_emp_g1` (both already wired) as a lens or an additional informed-arrival-adjacent signal, in place of the bare `usf_emp_g1 -1` lens.
  3. [method] Require the SC 13D leg to be an INITIAL filing or one with a RISING `percentOfClass` (the beneficial-ownership endpoint carries this), not any 13D/A amendment, so an exit does not register as arrival.

This is also the one archetype in the slice where the ALREADY-WIRED `esb_*` -> `evt_*` fill (lines 285-291, confirmed present in the current file, not a "future" layer for this specific gate) extends the core's reach beyond the roughly 2,000-name event-study subset to the ~17,500-name bulk-earnings universe — I confirmed the fill runs upstream of this archetype's definition (`fmp_earnings_bulk.csv` merged at line 285, `arch_mb_preprofit_beats_rewarded` defined at line 8418).

### arch_mb_quality_at_distress
- Spirit: MULTIBAGGER_UNCOVERED.md, "Covered profitable operators — 10x within 5 years": `max drawdown 2y low; EV/sales low; ROIC x FCF yield high; P/B vs sector low` (robust 9.2x, 52 events, 6 years, 6 markets, blow-up 27-29%; CLS 2020 37x, PRMB 2012 28x, EUZ.DE 2016, ARVIND 2020, DII-B.TO, WAWI.OL), and its `2y range high` twin (9.0x). Sister of `fallen_operator_industry_low` (C8) in the engine's own numbering.
- As coded now (line 7863-7869): `_mb_base & _operator` (`op_margin>=0 & fcf_margin>=0`, not asset-like) & `ts_dist_hi260<=0.5` & `_q_lo(_evsv)` (EV/sales bottom country quintile, `.where(ev_sales>0)`) & `_q_hi(_roce_x_fcfy)` where `_roce_x_fcfy = roce.clip(-1,1) * fcf_yield.clip(-1,1)` & `rel_ind_pb<=0.20`. Lenses (7): roce×fcfy (this time clipped 0-1, not -1..1 — see regression check) +1, fmp_altman_z +1, fq_netdebt_decline_months +1, ev_sales -1, rel_ind_pb -1, ts_dist_hi260 -1, ts_maxdd_5y -1. 32 firers, 0 exceptional, 0 elite (matches dumps3/CSV/live recompute).
- Regression check: PARTIALLY LANDED, WITH A GATE/LENS INCONSISTENCY. Audit-3 flagged (in the context of the sibling `tree_recipe`, whose lens uses the same product construction) that `roce.clip(-1,1) * fcf_yield.clip(-1,1)` lets a (-)x(-) pairing (a name with both negative ROCE and negative FCF yield) produce a large POSITIVE product that ranks ABOVE a modestly-profitable member — "the study's `op_roic_x_fcfy HIGH` was measured inside PROFITABLE operators where both factors are >= 0." The fix (dd7fb41) changed the CLIP BOUNDS from `(-1,1)` to `(0,1)` in the LENS definitions for both `tree_recipe` and `quality_at_distress` (comment: "(-)x(-) must not rank high") — but this archetype's own CORE GATE still computes `_roce_x_fcfy` with the OLD `.clip(-1,1)` bounds (line ~7866, unchanged) and uses THAT variable for the `_q_hi` cut that decides MEMBERSHIP, while the LENS (line 9835) separately recomputes the SAME quantity with the NEW `.clip(0,1)` bounds. The fix landed for ranking but not for the gate that decides who is in the box. I verified with a live recompute that this is currently DORMANT, not causing wrong members: all 32 current members have `roce>=0.022` and `fcf_yield>=0.073` (both strictly positive, verified via full_inner_df.pkl) — because `_operator` already requires `fcf_margin>=0`, which in practice keeps `fcf_yield>=0` too (same numerator sign, mcap always positive), so the (-)x(-) trap cannot currently trigger. This is a live, exploitable inconsistency (gate uses one formula, lens uses another) that happens not to matter today only because of an indirect sign relationship elsewhere in the core, not because it was actually fixed.
- Methodology issues:
  1. [confirmed above] Core gate (`clip(-1,1)`) and lens (`clip(0,1)`) for the same named quantity now disagree — a maintenance hazard even though currently harmless.
  2. The mined drawdown leg was a 2-YEAR max-drawdown / 2-year-range measure; the engine uses `ts_dist_hi260<=0.5` (a 5-year-high-relative snapshot) for the core AND `ts_maxdd_5y` (a 5-year window) for the lens — BOTH wrong horizon vs the source's stated 2-year window, and BOTH the same wrong horizon as each other, so at least the core and lens now at least agree on being off by the same amount (unresolved from audit-3, unchanged).

Audit-3's finding was that `~(fmp_st_shares_growth_3y>0.03)` let a NaN share-growth column PASS (a "fmp_filled_*"-adjacent no-op, since the fill flags are documented elsewhere in the file as "not values"). The fix (dd7fb41) built `_sh_g` as `fq_shares_yoy` FIRST, falling back to `fmp_st_shares_growth_3y` only where the quarterly figure is missing, and changed the comparison to a POSITIVE test (`_sh_g<=0.03`) that fails on NaN rather than an inverted negative test that passed on NaN. I verified with a live recompute that this now works exactly as intended: 0% of the 177 current members have a missing `fq_shares_yoy` (every member's "not diluting" status is measured from the quarterly panel directly, not merely inferred from an FY figure or, worse, assumed from a gap in the data) — "measured, not assumed," per the code's own comment, confirmed. Audit-3's OTHER suggestion — use `fq_equity<0` (72% coverage per the shared audit-3 facts) in place of the master `equity<0` (audit-3 stated 14% coverage) — did NOT land; `_stressed` still reads `_ncol('equity')<0` unchanged. ### arch_xr_amortization_mask
- Spirit: the serial-acquirer engine (Constellation / Heico class). Acquired-intangible amortisation has no cash cost but crushes GAAP EPS, so owner earnings run far above NI. The market prices the masked EPS while the cash compounds. Engine-native (code XR16). The nearest human screen is Pernas's "high D&A-to-capex" idea filter. Master reference II (Yartseva): FCF/P, not EPS, drives returns.
- As coded now (line 4861): goodwill+intangibles >= 30% of assets; NI > 0; OE/NI >= 1.5, where OE = NI + total D&A - max(capex_ttm, capex_avg); FCF yield >= 7%; P/E >= 15 or NaN; local mcap / OE <= 12; shares_yoy <= 5%; FX-coherent; not melting. There are no _tier / _reframe calls. Exceptional (10) and elite (0) come from the spirit-spec lens rank (goodwill share, P/E x OE yield, OE yield, FCF yield). Firers: 99 (pre3 99; 30 US).
- Regression check: audit 3 made no change to this gate (its fix went to the sibling depreciation_cliff, which now excludes goodwill share > 15%). The count is unchanged at 99. The P/E NaN escape admits 0 firers. The goodwill share is FMP-filled for 91 of 99 firers, so the gate is global in practice.

### arch_xr_discops_mask

Human sources: Wolf/Oak "Archetype 9: Turnaround/Structural Improvement" (disposal of unprofitable unit; catalyst: first improved earnings report; reject temporary restructuring charges/off-balance-sheet contingent liabilities); master ref I.C(6)/(19); Pernas "Low-multiple operational inflection."

  1. The divestiture is still never dated or confirmed — a "discontinued" line can be years stale (drag already gone) or an open-ended wind-down still consuming cash; no date/completion evidence exists in the gate.
  2. Leg A proves a consolidated loss with a profitable core but not its CAUSE — interest, tax, impairments inside continuing ops, or NCI on EDGAR rows can all produce the same pattern.
  3. On FMP-filled rows the continuing-income yield uses pre-NCI continuing income over parent-only mcap (overstates for majority-owned subs) — unresolved per the doc's lineage note.
  4. Wolf's own catalyst (first clean print post-disposal) is still absent although `fqx_eps_turned`/`fmp_dyn_*_turned_positive` exist elsewhere in the file.
  5. **USER RULE**: `(nde < 3.0) | (net_cash_pct_c >= 0)` has no source-stated number. Unlike a purely arbitrary bolt-on, Wolf's own text explicitly names "retained liabilities" as the trap for this specific archetype, so the CONCEPT of a leverage guard is closer to thesis-explicit here than in most of this slice's other flags — but the specific 3.0x threshold is still not a number the source states, so per the strict USER RULE wording it is still flagged as a candidate for `_DEMOTED`, with the caveat that the concept itself (not just the number) has real source support.
- Where the new layers apply: none of esb_/fg_/evh_ measures a discontinued-ops line directly; the doc's own FMP augmentation (`fq_disc_ops_share`, global, already present for 89 of 104 in the doc's cohort but UNUSED as the natural global form of leg B) remains the correct global-reach fix and is not one of the three new layers.

## Slice summary — the ten most valuable findings across all 26 xr_a archetypes (audit 4)

1. [method] **USER RULE: seven ancillary leverage/quality caps remain live gates with no source-stated number**, all structurally identical to patterns c99761f already demoted elsewhere in this same file: asset_owner_catalyst (`nde<3.0`), baron_compounder (`nde<=2.0`), cannibal_below_tbook (`nde<3.0` AND a bolt-on `roce>=0.05` floor — the same category as the already-removed `book_compounder` ROE floor), cyclical_trough (`nde<3.5`, positive-EBITDA branch), double_trough (`interest_coverage>=4`/`nde<=1.5`, positive-EBITDA branch), discops_mask (`nde<3.0`, with a partial Wolf-sourced concept but no sourced number), forced_seller (`nde<3.0`). All seven should move to `_DEMOTED` weights. The negative-EBITDA balance-sheet SUBSTITUTES in cyclical_trough/double_trough are correctly protected as measured-not-assumed data-validity fixes and are NOT flagged.
2. [data] **A materiality fix silently converted two global gates into near-US-only ones.** cannibal_below_cash and cannibal_below_tbook both now require `buyback_yield>=0.01` as a MANDATORY leg; `buyback_yield` notna share is 21.6% for US vs 0.15% for non-US (verified on asymmetry_global.csv). This explains most of the 67.5%/70% firer collapses in these two archetypes and reverses the doc's own stated intent (materiality, not exclusivity). Fix: add a global `fq buyback flow / mcap >= 0.01` OR-alternative (fx-bridged), not one of the three new incoming layers.
3. [method] **The same "hidden-asset floor collapses to net cash" bug appears in three archetypes** (asset_owner_catalyst, floor_inflection, forensic_floor_growth) and remains unfixed in all three despite being documented in audit 3 for at least two of them. Fix once, apply to all three: count the hidden-asset leg only where associates are observed.
4. [method] **Three zero-drift gates received none of the audit-3 doc's own suggestions**: floor_inflection (720=720), forensic_floor_growth (839=839), cash_leads_book (549=549, though this one's core design was already sound per the doc). floor_inflection and forensic_floor_growth in particular carry the slice's largest remaining spirit gaps (undated "inflection," a floor that is not a floor) untouched since the doc was written — these should be the next fixes prioritized, ahead of re-auditing already-fixed archetypes.
5. [method] **confluence's 51% count collapse (1,568->774) is a legitimate cascade**, not a new bug: the "engine" family now excludes audited_streak_unrerated and gaap_profit_crossover entirely (verified: neither name appears in any of the four `_XR_FAMILIES` lists, a more complete fix than the inline comment implies), compounding with independent tightening in asset_owner_catalyst/cannibal_below_cash/cannibal_below_tbook/clean_net_net/compounding_deployer/deferred_revenue_lead/depreciation_cliff/discops_mask/baron_compounder. The doc's own top unresolved item — `beaten_down_any` sitting inside multiple counted families, letting one crash light more than one family — is still open and is now the highest-value remaining fix for this archetype specifically.
6. [spirit] **The D&A-vs-amortisation conflation appears in four archetypes** (amortization_mask, depreciation_cliff — now fenced from goodwill>15% and collapsed 22->6 as a result — forensic_floor_growth, forensic_multiple_gap), with the fence landed in only one of the four. Propagate the same `fq_gw_pct_assets` guard to forensic_floor_growth's third leg and forensic_multiple_gap's OE construction.
7. [method] **forensic_multiple_gap's audit-3 cash-confirmation fix changed the doc's own proposed formula**: the doc asked for `fq_cfo_to_ni>=0.8x(OE/NI)` (wedge-proportional); the code implements a flat `fq_cfo_to_ni>=1.0` (wedge-independent) — a different claim than what was proposed, and one that does not itself deduct SBC, so an SBC-inflated CFO can now pass the very leg meant to prove the wedge is real cash.
8. [data] **New-layer mapping, the three highest-value placements**: (a) `evh_evs_log_chg_1y`/`evh_evs_vs_med_3y` should become the CORE "not re-rated"/"unpriced" test for audited_streak_unrerated, forced_seller, gaap_profit_crossover and gross_margin_lead (four archetypes currently proving "unpriced" only by an absolute valuation band, never by the name's own multiple history); (b) `esb_beats_8q`/`esb_react_beats_4q`/`esb_ignored_beats_2y` should supply the "told" half missing from audited_streak_unrerated and the dated-catalyst evidence missing from asset_owner_catalyst/floor_inflection; (c) `fg_ocf_ps_5y`/`fg_rev_ps_5y`/`fg_*_min5` should replace or corroborate every snapshot-based "compounding"/"survived the cycle" claim (amortization_mask, baron_compounder, compounding_deployer, cyclical_trough, double_trough, clean_net_net's NCAV-trend gap).
9. [method] **Snapshot-vs-panel and single-vs-multi-statistic conflations recur across the slice**: baron_compounder mixes a 36-month EDGAR duration window with a 24-month fq fill under one "12 quarters" label; forced_seller's "business grew" leg mixes master `rev_yoy` with panel `fqx_ebit_ttm_g`/`fq_rev_growth` inconsistently across its own legs; deferred_revenue_lead's `fq_defrev_growth_minus_rev` plays three different, none-mandatory roles in one gate; cash_tax_advantage runs two different persistence standards (1 TTM window vs >=2 FY median) across its two paths. None of these are new findings, but none have been resolved since the doc either.
10. [spirit] **gross_margin_lead is the one leg in this slice where the human source states an exact number the code understates**: Andreola-Deden's own gate requires revenue growth >25%; the code requires only >=5%. Tightening toward the sourced figure (or explicitly surfacing the gap on the book) is a rare case here of a genuine SOURCE-NUMBER gate available but unused, the inverse of most other findings in this slice (arbitrary numbers with NO source, rather than a real source number left unused).

## Slice summary: the ten most valuable augmentations (ranked)
1. [method, highest value] Fix the `data_quality_flag` forward-reference no-op: the column is computed once at line 9153, thousands of lines after 14 of this slice's 26 archetypes read `df.get('data_quality_flag', 0) == 0` as a supposed post-audit-3 fix (neg_ev_growth 4515, triple_floor 4531, wc_normalization 4847, latent_bath_floor 5182, nol_shield 5262, oneoff_loss_mask 5374, hidden_segment_compounder 5455, segment_justifies_whole 5471, margin_mixshift 5505, owned_realestate_value 5658, investment_remark 5808, stake_fv_gap 5817, lookthrough_earner 5834, value_unlock ~5871). Proven on the data with a zero-other-change control case (`xr_segment_justifies_whole`: 73 firers audit-3, 73 firers now, byte-identical count). Move the DQ computation (or a lightweight proxy) before line ~4100.
2. [spirit] Wire `nol_usd` (already computed and used by the sibling `xr_monetization_trifecta`) into `xr_nol_shield`'s gate as the direct tax-loss-bank corroboration — the archetype currently infers a "shield" from a book-level `retained_earnings` deficit alone, which is not a tax-loss-bank proxy, while the direct EDGAR measure sits unused two archetypes away.
3. [method] `xr_monetization_trifecta` collapsed from 5 firers to 1 after stacking a new `net_income_ttm>0` requirement ON TOP OF the pre-existing `ebitda_margin>0.03` leg (reconstructed funnel: 176 candidates -> 21 after NI>0 alone). Resolve whether both profitability floors are intended or redundant before the archetype becomes permanently inert (n=1 means the spirit-tiering machinery's own >=5-member rule can never fire).
4. [data] `xr_look_through_value` and `xr_lookthrough_earner` both show their firer-set's US/non-US composition FLIPPING between audit-3 and now despite `xr_look_through_value` having zero code changes — a producer-file (`investment_remark.csv`) snapshot-drift effect, not a code fix. Any book/report characterising these as "US-only" should be re-verified against the current data before republishing, and the drift itself should be understood before more fixes are layered on top of a moving target.
5. [spirit] The segment-margin leg that actually defines "hidden compounder"/"mix-shift" (`fastest_seg_opmargin_delta_yoy`, `seg_margin_inflect_flag`, `seg_oplev`, `seg_mix_uplift`) remains EDGAR/US-only in `xr_hidden_segment_compounder` and `xr_margin_mixshift`, even though the REVENUE-side legs (`fastest_segment_yoy`, `segment_count`, `fastest_segment_share[_delta]`) were successfully globalised via the `_fmp_fill` coalesce with `fmp_segments.csv` (lines 463-479) — FMP has no segment-level EBIT/margin field, so this specific gap needs a different data source, not just more wiring of the existing one.
6. [method, positive finding] `xr_paydown_yield`'s `_nde_meaningful>0` leg, with the explicit comment "(user) debt exists to pay down (no fixed band)," is the clearest evidence in this slice that the c99761f leverage-cap removal was a deliberate, considered USER RULE decision rather than an oversight — worth citing as the model pattern when reviewing whether a similar cap belongs elsewhere (e.g. `xr_verified_deleveraging`'s nde 1.5-4.0 band, `xr_nol_shield`'s shares<=8%, both left as-is and not flagged as violations here since they are thesis-tied, not arbitrary).
7. [method] `xr_verified_deleveraging` and `xr_paydown_yield` both still mix two DIFFERENT debt definitions in the same gate — the dated path (`fq_deleveraging_flag`, FMP `totalDebt`) vs the level band (`nde`, provider debt) — so a name can pass the path and fail (or vice-versa) the level for reasons unrelated to the actual deleveraging. Reconciling `nde` onto the FMP `totalDebt` figure the path already uses is a single producer-side change that would tighten both archetypes at once.
8. [spirit] `xr_wc_normalization`'s audit-3 rewrite (replacing `cash_conversion<0.7` with the `cfo_yield<earnings_yield-3pp`-plus-mechanism / direct-glut-observed pair, and the Beneish/receivables-divergence veto) is the cleanest, most completely executed fix set found in this slice (350->157 firers, fully explained by the removal of a leg that fired on 57% of the old population with no observed WC build) — worth using as the template when revisiting looser proxy-based legs elsewhere (e.g. `xr_oneoff_loss_mask`'s CFO-NI-without-D&A leg, which attempted the same kind of fix but landed weaker than specified).
9. [method] `xr_owned_realestate_value` still gates on ALL of PP&E (machinery, vehicles, fixtures), not specifically land/buildings, so it continues to substantially duplicate `arch_overdepreciated_assets`'s thesis (76% of its 33 current firers also carry `arch_hidden_assets`-adjacent flags per the look-through-value overlap check, and the land/buildings EDGAR tags audit-3 proposed remain unadded) — the single highest-value, still-fully-open data fix named across two audit rounds now.
10. [data] Where esb_*/fg_*/evh_* would help most in this slice: `fg_bvps_up_share5`/`fg_rev_ps_3y_pos_share5` as a genuinely global second quality lens for `xr_quality_crisis` (closing its single-weak-lens gap using data now on hand); `evh_evs_vs_med_3y` as an own-history "not yet repriced" corroboration across the whole mismark/stake family (`xr_investment_remark`, `xr_look_through_value`, `xr_lookthrough_earner`, `xr_stake_fv_gap`, `xr_hidden_segment_compounder`, `xr_value_unlock`) where today each relies on a static snapshot cheapness OR; esb_* is a poor fit for most of this slice's balance-sheet/segment/mismark theses and its best use is `xr_leverage_detonation`/`xr_peer_margin_gap`'s dated-crossing corroboration.

## Audit 4 — slice rest_a (37 single archetypes, A): forensic re-read of `archetype_tags.py` at 39fc934 (625c104 wired esb/fg/evh; 39fc934 removed the fallen-angel leverage cap and `fallen_angel_levered_flag`), with the three new layers as proposed augmentations

Counts are from the on-disk `archetype_tags.csv` / `archetype_tiers.csv` (written 09:13, i.e. BEFORE 625c104: no `per_share_compounder_flag`, no esb fill of `earnings_beat_rate`), joined with the overlays in `audit4/merged.pkl`; where 625c104 changes a count I simulate the new leg on the same data and say so. `fmp_ev_history.csv` is NOT on disk yet, so every `evh_*` read is all-NaN today (a no-op, not a bug); `fmp_financial_growth.csv` is on disk (29,250 rows, still being written). Nothing here is a back-test.

**Cross-cutting finding (verified, affects 7 archetypes in this slice: analyst_awakening, analyst_rerating_confirmed, asleep_at_wheel, asleep_unrerated, blindspot, evsales_derating, flyover).** For every `_tier`-ed archetype that also has a `_SPIRIT` entry, the spirit loop at lines 9970-9994 OVERWRITES `<name>_exceptional` and `<name>_elite` with `spirit >= 0.75` / `>= 0.90` (line 9974 `elif _n in _TIERED and _n in _SPIRIT`), and `_pre_exc` (line 9967) deliberately excludes `_TIERED` names, so the qualitative `exceptional=` and `elite_metric=` arguments passed to `_tier(...)` are dead code. Evidence: analyst_awakening's coded exceptional (`evt_pt_lead_flag == 1 | _sent_turn_n >= 2`) holds for 322 of 1,674 core names; the file has 24 exceptional (20 overlap) and 1 elite, because only 770 core names carry >= 3 of the 5 spirit lenses and a mean of within-core percentile ranks >= 0.75 is rare. asleep_unrerated: coded exceptional (`evt_react_beats_4q <= 0`) holds for 248 core names, the file has 65. Every audit-3 "exceptional:" sentence written into a `_tier` call in this slice is therefore not what the books print. One-line fix: in the spirit loop, `df[_n+'_exceptional'] |= _tier_exc[_n]` for `_TIERED` names (store the `_tier` exceptional before the loop, as `_pre_exc` does for the others), and keep `_tier`'s elite_metric where it was given.

[verified, landed] The dilution guard (`~(shares_growth_5y>0.05)`, audit-3 suggestion 1 "TOTAL equity compounding on issuance is not book-per-share compounding") is present and correct. 2. [verified, revised after checking `docs/spirit_spec.json` directly] Audit-3's own fix "a financial member must still earn on its book" (`~(is_financial & roe<0.08)`) was REMOVED by c99761f as a non-thesis gate, defensible under the USER RULE taken alone (0.08 is not the source's own number — Tillinghast's cited source text says ROE>10-12%, a HIGHER bar than the removed 8% floor). There is NO `_DEMOTED.setdefault('book_compounder_discount', ...)` call anywhere in the file (confirmed by a full-file grep for every `_DEMOTED.setdefault(` call), so the specific 25%-weighted "former gate" blend the commit describes does NOT apply here. However — checking `docs/spirit_spec.json` directly (not just the dump's boilerplate excerpt) — `book_compounder_discount` DOES carry an explicit spec entry with lenses `[equity_cagr_5y(+1), roe(+1), pos(pb)(-1), pos(p_tb)(-1)]`, and `_SPIRIT_ALL` includes every `_SPEC` name whose `arch_` column exists (confirmed in the spirit-computation loop, lines 9951-9987) — so `roe` DOES already carry full (non-demoted, ~25%-of-4-lenses) weight in the ordinary spirit score via the pre-existing generic spec, not because of anything c99761f added. Net effect is milder than a first read of the `_DEMOTED` registry suggests: a financial member with low or negative ROE will rank POORLY on that lens (hurting its spirit score and its odds of being "exceptional," `sc>=0.75`) but will still be a base-tier MEMBER as long as NI is positive — the hard FLOOR is gone (correctly, per the USER RULE) and what remains is a RELATIVE rank, which is the intended "gate -> weight" outcome, just delivered through the pre-existing spec rather than a fresh `_DEMOTED` entry.

[still open per audit-3] Mixed total-vs-per-share definitions persist at the boundary: EDGAR names use TOTAL equity CAGR (can pass on a rights issue that grows total equity while diluting per-share value) while the fg fallback is genuinely per-share — so an EDGAR-covered US name and an FMP-covered global name are held to two different definitions of "compounding" under the same 8% cut, exactly as audit-3 flagged, and the fg fix (line 4437) only ADDS a better global fallback, it does not fix the EDGAR path's own total-equity flaw. 3. `_not_melting` is permissive (NaN op_margin) for banks/insurers per audit-3's still-open note — a financial member with no measured `op_margin` (common for lenders, whose profitability lives in NIM, not op_margin) sails through this survivability guard by default. 4. ### arch_coiled_base
- Spirit: engine theory + base-breakout event study (cited inline, lines 7329-7337): a future multi-bagger goes nowhere for ~2 years (the COIL — value accretes while price does not), the market is not watching or does not believe (PERCEPTION LAG), and when the first buyers arrive (IGNITION, covered under `base_ignition`) the stock moves fast because earnings growth and multiple expansion land together. ## 10-line ranked slice summary (slice rest_b, 37 archetypes, re-audited at HEAD c99761f)

1. **`arch_qarp` has a live code-correctness bug, not just a magnitude issue**: the audit-3 fix meant to replace the loose `_qarp_cheap` single-lens OR with a "2-of-3-agree, or EV/EBIT<=12 alone" test instead added the new test ALONGSIDE the old one (both still ANDed) -- the intended EV/EBIT-alone escape is neutered because it still must also clear the old `_qarp_cheap` OR. Verified with data: 104 universe names have EV/EBIT<=12 but fail `_qarp_cheap` and are wrongly excluded. Fix: delete the leftover `_qarp_cheap` AND-term.
2. **`arch_strong_coverage` (8645 firers, the broadest archetype in this slice) gates on an unsourced 8x interest-coverage number while its own cited source (Tillinghast) states a specific, different, unused threshold: Debt/EBITDA>4x = "scary."** The archetype never tests Debt/EBITDA at all. This is the largest-population USER-RULE source-number mismatch found in the slice, and audit-3's own two still-open suggestions (tier it / demote to a flag) would resolve the archetype's parallel "not a mispricing" self-critique in the same stroke.
3. **The ETR-globalization fix (`effective_tax_rate.fillna(fmp_effective_tax_rate)`, shared between `tax_efficient` and `tax_verified_earnings`) is this slice's cleanest, most impactful, correctly-executed fix**: coverage genuinely expanded from ~5% (US-only by data accident) toward FMP's ~82% global reach, producing count jumps of +865% and +681% respectively, both fully explained and verified -- a positive counter-example to the missing-data-direction bugs found elsewhere.
4. **A recurring "measured-veto, near-zero-coverage" bug pattern appears at least four times**: `hidden_assets`' associate-stake veto (29/1955 measured, 0 excluded), `insider_conviction`'s dollar size-floor (22/565 measured, 0 excluded), and `understated_earnings`' SBC-pollution veto (115/1996 measured, 0 excluded) are all verified no-ops or near-no-ops -- the intent lands as code but the underlying column's sparse coverage (frequently EDGAR-only) means the veto currently excludes nobody. This is a systemic data-reach problem, not three unrelated bugs.
5. **`arch_tangible_value` is the cleanest confirmed "bug fix worked as intended" case**: replacing the raw `nde<=4` leverage test (which FAILED every negative-EBITDA name on the 99-fill, excluding exactly the loss-making-asset-rich names the archetype exists to find) with the NaN-aware `_lev_ok(4.0)` caused the count to RISE 13.6% despite two new AND-legs -- direct, count-level proof the fix re-admitted wrongly-excluded names while a well-covered new Altman-Z veto (91.9% coverage, 0 violations) trimmed the worst of them.
6. **`arch_levered_inflection`'s leverage band does not match its own cited source**: Wolf/Oak Archetype 8 states ND/EBITDA 1.5-3x trending down; the coded `heavy_debt` floor (>=3x) actually EXCLUDES the source's own sweet spot, and the audit-3-era cap (now 8x) is 2.6x looser than the source's stated ceiling -- the archetype currently screens a 3-8x band that barely overlaps the thesis it claims.
7. **`arch_sustainable_scaler` has the densest concentration of loosened-vs-source-stated numbers of any single archetype**: mcap<$2bn vs Andreola-Deden's stated <$300M, EV/S<=8 vs the source's <3x, and a 15% growth floor vs the compendium's stated >=25% -- three separate, independently-verifiable source-number mismatches in one gate, alongside three genuinely well-landed audit-3 fixes (missing-share-history, earnings-growing, net-cash-or-light-leverage).
8. **`arch_owner_operator`'s new core-tier ceiling (50%) doesn't match its own source's explicit range (insider ownership "20-58% in the best cases")** -- a precise, verifiable one-number mismatch on an otherwise well-targeted, correctly-landed audit-3 fix (which also fixed a genuine US/global FCF-bar asymmetry).
9. **Baseline universe/data drift of roughly 30-50%, independent of any code fix, is confirmed and should discount raw count deltas throughout this whole audit**: `regime_cyclical`'s preserved OLD-rule population (`_watch`) recomputes to 1538 today vs audit-3's own reported 1038 for the BYTE-IDENTICAL rule -- meaning count-based regression checks are only reliable when cross-checked against actual leg-level violation counts (as done for most archetypes in this file), not read as fix-attributable on their own.
10. **Several archetypes received zero attention since audit-3 despite still-open, previously-identified problems**: `pension_overfunded`, `post_reorg`, `special_situation`, `lifo_hidden_reserve`, `low_sbc_quality`, `quiet_compounder`'s neglect/price gaps, and `narrative_lag` are all byte-identical (or functionally identical) to their audit-3 state -- `post_reorg` in particular still prices Verdad's emergence-yield thesis on TODAY's price at half the source's stated 20% threshold, a compounding of the "wrong date" and "wrong number" problems audit-3 already named.

### arch_bab_becoming
- Spirit: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014) "Betting Against Beta" (not in the five uploaded documents; engine comment block, line 2575-2590): alpha = psi(1 - beta), long safe, profitable low-beta assets. "Becoming" is the engine's own extension: a name whose beta is compressing toward the low-beta long leg before the market re-labels it. F&P define no compression rule; the compendium has no BAB entry.
- As coded now (reframed, line 2735): is_operating; revenue_ttm_usd >= $20M; fcf_margin > -5%; `_roce_now_ok`; rev_yoy > -5%; op_margin > 0 (audit 3); nde <= 3 (99-filled); `_compress` = [1y within-market beta rank <= 3y rank - 0.10 OR (1y vol / 3y vol) / market-median ratio <= 0.85 (audit 3, market-relative)] AND 3y rank > 0.35 AND panel 3y beta > 0. Old rule = `bab_becoming_watch` (1,729); Yahoo-band proxy where no panel beta = `bab_becoming_proxy_watch` (136). Spirit lenses: 3y rank - 1y rank, 1 - vol1y/vol3y, ebitda_margin_delta_yoy. 1,962 core (pre-audit-3 2,357), 66 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: (1) market-relative vol leg landed (`_vratio.groupby(country).transform('median')`, `country` = `src`, line 854); 420 of 1,962 firers are vol-only. 11 firers sit in markets with < 50 vol-ratio names, where the median is noisy; one market's median is 0.0 (the `.where(_vratio_mkt > 0)` guard sends it to the beta path, correct). (2) op_margin > 0 landed. (3) The proxy demotion landed (136 proxy_watch; the core has no Yahoo path). No no-op, no inverted sign. Count 2,357 -> 1,962 is the intended tightening.
- Methodology issues:
  1. [verified] The beta-rank leg is at the noise floor. Across the universe the median |ts_beta_1y_rk - ts_beta_3y_rk| is 0.106, i.e. the "fell >= 10 points" bar is the typical one-year wobble of a rank; 1,542 of 1,962 firers pass on it. Firers' current 1y rank has median 0.48 (IQR 0.31-0.64): most "becoming low-beta" names are still mid-beta. The leg measures rank churn, not compression.
  2. [verified] `nde <= 3.0` reads the 99 fill: of 3,056 names passing every other core leg, 262 fail only because net_debt_ebitda is NaN (op_margin > 0, so these are unfetched-net-debt names, not loss-makers). `_lev_ok(3.0)` exists for exactly this (audit-3 mechanism 1) and is not used here or in `bab_quality` (nde <= 2.5).

  2. [method] Replace `nde <= 3.0` with `_lev_ok(3.0)` in the core and in `bab_becoming_proxy_watch` (262 names).
  3. [method] Vol leg only in markets with >= 50 measured ratios (else the beta leg alone).
  4. [data] `fg_ocf_ps_5y_min5 > 0` where measured as the fundamental "becoming safe" corroboration (NaN-permissive).

[verified] The within-market beta rank is taken over every listed name, and the low-beta third is dominated by non-trading artifacts: in the US the names with ts_beta_3y_rk <= 0.35 have median mcap $54M against $460M for all ranked US names. Suggestion #1 (rank both legs within the investable universe, combined rank<=decile/quartile, instead of absolute cuts) did NOT land — the gate is still two absolute cuts (0.10, 0.25/[0.20,1.0]). Suggestion #3 (put both ROC lenses on the same pre-/after-tax basis before one threshold) did NOT land — `roce` (pre-tax) and `fqx_roic_ttm` (after-tax) still sit under two separately-calibrated absolute cuts. The `~_roce_oneoff_suspect` veto is a new, unlisted addition (tagged "(audit)" not "(audit 3)") that closes a real tiny-denominator artifact by reusing an existing helper — a good, low-risk fix. Firer count moved only 763(A1-era)->759, consistent with the EV-sanity/mcap tightening catching very few names (as expected, since magic-formula candidates are rarely EV-corrupt shells) — no collapse or unexplained swing.
- Methodology issues:
  1. [USER RULE, central] Greenblatt's method is explicitly RANK-based, not threshold-based ("rank the universe... buy the best COMBINED rank"); the code substitutes two absolute magnitude cuts (EBIT/EV>=10%, ROCE>=25%) approximating "top quartile"/"top decile-ish" (the engine's own comment's hedge words). Neither "10%" nor "25%" is a number Greenblatt's book states — they are regime-dependent approximations that audit-3 already flagged (unresolved suggestion #1) as causing membership to "swing with the rate regime," and a name can be 1st percentile on one leg and 60th on the other and still fire. This is the clearest, most structural USER RULE case in this archetype: the gate mechanism itself (absolute cut) is not what the source specifies (relative rank).
  2. [unresolved, audit-3 #1] `roce` (provider EBIT/(total assets - current liabilities), includes goodwill and cash) is not Greenblatt's own denominator (net working capital + net fixed assets, excluding both) — an acquisitive name with a large goodwill base or a cash-rich name reads LOW on `roce`, the OPPOSITE bias from the paper's intended tangible-capital measure.
  3. [unresolved, audit-3 #3] The two ROC paths are different statistics under one implicit "good" label: pre-tax `roce` at a 25% cut vs after-tax `fqx_roic_ttm` at a [20%,100%] band assuming a flat ~20% tax rate translates to "~25% pre-tax" for every market — a single conversion factor applied globally.
  4. [unresolved, audit-3 #2, partial] The 100% upper cap on `fqx_roic_ttm` drops genuinely capital-light franchises (royalties, software) the Magic Formula is specifically meant to surface, while the `roce` path has no such cap (asymmetric treatment of the same "too good to be true" concern across the two ROC paths).
- New layers: `evh_ev_ebit_log_chg_1y` / `evh_ev_mcap_ratio` would strengthen or replace `_ev_sane`'s single-snapshot EV-sanity check with a dated, historically-aware EV read once `fmp_ev_history.csv` exists. `fg_*` per-share growth series are not obviously on-thesis here (Magic Formula is a static-year rank, not a growth thesis) — n/a. `esb_*` — n/a.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Per USER RULE and audit-3 suggestion #1 (still open): compute a combined percentile rank of EBIT/EV and ROC within the investable (is_operating, mcap>=$50M, EV-sane) universe, and gate on the combined rank (e.g., top decile = core) instead of the two absolute cuts — this is the single highest-value fix since it replaces an un-sourced gate mechanism with the source's own actual method.
  2. [method] Compute ROC on Greenblatt's own tangible-capital denominator (NWC + net fixed assets, from `fq` balance-sheet lines) globally, per audit-3 suggestion #4/FMP augmentation, rather than the biased `roce` proxy (issue 2).
  3. [method] Put `roce` and `fqx_roic_ttm` on the same pre-/after-tax basis before applying one threshold (issue 3), per audit-3 suggestion #3, still open.
  4. [method] Drop or raise the 100% `fqx_roic_ttm` cap asymmetry (issue 4) so capital-light franchises aren't excluded on one ROC path but not the other.
- EVERY PERSPECTIVE checklist: 1) Fidelity — EBIT/EV and financials/utilities exclusion are captured; the RANK mechanism (the paper's actual method) is not (issue 1); the tangible-capital ROC denominator is not (issue 2); one-year hold/rebalance is out of scope for a snapshot screener (acceptable, not a fidelity bug). 2) Gate legitimacy — mcap>=$50M is Greenblatt's own cited floor (keep); the 10%/25%/[20,100%] cuts are all un-sourced approximations of a rank the source never reduces to absolute numbers (issue 1, the central USER RULE finding of this section). 3) Lineage — ev_ebit/roce are M snapshot ratios (single-period, provider-defined, currency-neutral by construction since ev_ebit is local/local); fqx_roic_ttm is FQX (global, after-tax, quarterly panel). Two different vintages and tax bases under one "ROC" label (issue 3). 4) Coverage — global by construction (no US-only leg identified); `_ev_sane` protects against a specific cross-listing artifact (ADR/.F lines) rather than restricting geography. 5) Missing-data direction — not separately traced for `_greenblatt_ey`/`roce`/`fqx_roic_ttm` in this pass; worth a follow-up read of `_greenblatt_ey`'s construction (`1/ev_ebit`) for its own NaN/zero handling, not done here. 6) Units/currency — `ev_ebit` is explicitly local EV/local EBIT (currency-neutral, verified via audit-3's own lineage note) — clean, no cross-currency risk found. 7) Definitions — issue 3 (pre-tax vs after-tax ROC under one implicit "good" bar) is exactly a "two statistics, one threshold" case. 8) Code correctness — none found; `_ev_sane`, `mcap>=50e6`, and `_roce_oneoff_suspect` were all traced to real, correctly-reused helpers, not new inline logic prone to a fresh bug. 9) Regression — covered above (mcap/EV fix landed cleanly with a near-flat count change; two suggestions remain open; no collapse). 10) Tiers/weights — not spirited, no `_tier()`; exceptional (44)/elite (4) via the generic unspirited mechanism, not traced further. 11) Overlap — not checked against other "cheap and good" archetypes in the file (e.g., `cheap_per_roiic`, `midcap_garp` — the latter is explicitly named in audit-3's methodology issue #3 as already having its own EV-sanity guard, implying some sibling-archetype logic duplication across the file that was not itself checked for double-counting here). 12) New layers — covered above (evh_ev_ebit_log_chg_1y, evh_ev_mcap_ratio; fg_*/esb_* n/a).

### arch_kullamagie_breakout
- Spirit: Kristjan Kullamägi's published setup (qullamaggie.com, not in the five uploaded documents): the strongest stocks by 1/3/6-month performance ("top 1-2%"), a prior move of 30-100%+, an orderly 2-8-week consolidation with a tightening range and volume drying up, above rising 10/20-day MAs, entry on the opening-range high with the stop at the low of day; the episodic-pivot (EP) variant is a 10%+ earnings gap on huge volume; he trades liquid names only. Engine comment: "[C] leader across momentum scans; [C] large prior advance (>=30%); [P] orderly tightening near rising highs."
- As coded now: watch (snapshot-only, global percentile) = live tape; leader (>=95th global pct on 6m/12m momentum); impulse (max(roc_6m,mom12)>=30%); tight (monthly squeeze run>=3 OR 12-month base depth<=35%); near (0.5%-25% off 52w high). Core (`_tier`, line 3257-3261, where panel RS exists): `ts_rs_pct_mkt>=90` (within-market, not global); (audit 3) `ts_dist_hi52>=0.90` (replacing the 0.75/"25%-off" bar the audit-3 comment itself calls "a base, not a breakout"); above the 30-week MA; `ts_dvol26_usd>=$1M/week`; (audit 3) `~_clin_bio_e` (clinical-biotech exclusion). Exceptional: RS>=95, `ts_tight5<=0.10` (5-week range), `>=$5M/week`. Lenses: ts_rs_raw(+), ts_tight5(-), ts_dist_hi52(+), ts_dvol26_usd(+). 305 core, 1,166 watch, 2 exceptional, 0 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 suggestion #3 (core near-high = `ts_dist_hi52>=0.90`) landed exactly as written, verified in the code with the identical rationale comment. The clinical-biotech exclusion (methodology issue #3, "92 firers... in a binary-event mechanism") landed as `~_clin_bio_e` in the core `_tier` condition — a direct, verified fix (simpler than audit-3's own suggestion of routing to a separate `biotech_momentum_watch`, but it resolves the leak). Suggestion #1 (make tightness core, not exceptional) did NOT land — `ts_tight5<=0.10` is still exceptional-only; the core has no tightness/duration test at all. Suggestion #2 (volume dry-up lens) did NOT land — no such lens exists among the four listed. The $1M/week core liquidity floor (methodology issue #2, "far below the liquidity he requires") is unchanged. No inversion, no forward reference; the near-high tightening (0.75->0.90) plausibly explains at least part of any core-count reduction versus an earlier pass, though no single audit-3 baseline number was quoted in the doc excerpt to compare against directly.
- Methodology issues:
  1. [new finding, fidelity gap] Kullamägi's own stated bar is "top 1-2%" of the momentum universe; the core gates on `ts_rs_pct_mkt>=90` (top 10%, within-market) and even the exceptional tier only reaches >=95 (top 5%) — both materially looser than the source's literal "1-2%" figure, with no documented rationale for the gap (breadth/reach is a plausible reason but is not stated in-code).
  2. [unresolved, audit-3 #1] Two different percentile bases feed "leader": the watch uses a GLOBAL percentile (over-weighting a few markets 2-7x per audit-3's own measurement) while the core uses a within-market percentile — only the core, not the watch, was fixed.
  3. [unresolved, audit-3 #2] Core liquidity floor ($1M/week) is well below what Kullamägi actually trades; audit-3 found 18% of watch firers under $1M/week even against that floor.
  4. [unresolved, audit-3, Fidelity list] No 2-8-week consolidation DURATION test exists anywhere in core or watch — a name breaking out after a 14-month base and a name breaking out after a textbook 4-week flag are treated identically.
  5. [unresolved, audit-3, Fidelity list] No volume-dry-up (VDU) lens — "orderly tightening... volume drying up" is only half-represented (the range-tightening half, exceptional-only per issue 1's sibling finding); the volume half has no proxy at all.
- New layers: `esb_react_last` / `esb_pead_4w` (post-earnings price reaction/drift, universe-wide) is the natural building block for the still-missing episodic-pivot (EP) variant (a 10%+ earnings gap on huge volume) — audit-3 suggestion #4, still open, and now buildable globally rather than needing a dedicated `earnings`-dates pull. `fg_*` — n/a (this is a pure tape/momentum thesis, not a fundamentals one). `evh_*` — n/a.
- Suggestions:
  1. [method] Raise the core/exceptional leadership bar toward the source's literal "top 1-2%" (e.g., core >=95th, exceptional >=98th within-market) per issue 1, or explicitly document why 90th/95th was chosen instead.
  2. [spirit] Per audit-3 suggestion #1 (still open): make `ts_tight5<=0.10` (or a weekly-range-contraction lens) part of the CORE, with a 2-10-week duration band since the impulse high, not exceptional-only.
  3. [spirit] Per audit-3 suggestion #2 (still open): add a volume-dry-up lens (e.g., last-4-week volume / 26-week median <= 0.7) from the TS panel.
  4. [data] Build the EP variant from `esb_react_last`/`esb_pead_4w` (a large, high-volume post-earnings reaction) per audit-3 suggestion #4, now feasible globally via the new earnings-bulk layer instead of a dedicated `earnings`-dates pull.
  5. [method] Fix the watch's global (not within-market) percentile per audit-3 #1, still open.
- EVERY PERSPECTIVE checklist: 1) Fidelity — leadership percentile (issue 1), consolidation duration (issue 4), and volume dry-up (issue 5) are the three source elements least faithfully captured; the prior-impulse ">=30%" floor is captured faithfully and matches the source's own number (keep). 2) Gate legitimacy — the ">=30%" impulse floor is source-cited (keep); the 90th/95th percentile cuts (issue 1) and the $1M/$5M liquidity floors (issue 3) are engine approximations of qualitative-but-numbered source language ("top 1-2%," "liquid names only") without matching the source's own figure — borderline, not a clean invented-from-nothing gate but not a correctly-cited one either. 3) Lineage — watch legs are stale YF/lynch-tape snapshots (per audit-3's own "momentum noise 27-29%" note, unresolved); core/tier/exceptional legs are the dated weekly TS panel (global, USD-quote-unit aware) — two very different data-quality tiers feeding the same archetype name. 4) Coverage — global by construction; the within-market vs global percentile split (issue 2) is the main geography-shaped inconsistency, affecting the watch population's market mix, not the core's. 5) Missing-data direction — the `_tier`'s `measured=ts_rs_pct_mkt.notna() & ts_dist_hi52.notna()` pass-through means a name without panel RS data is judged on the (looser, global-percentile) watch rule alone — same "patchy coverage is never a requirement" design seen elsewhere, not a bug. 6) Units/currency — `ts_dvol26_usd` is explicitly USD-normalized and quote-unit aware per the audit-3 lineage note; no currency risk found. 7) Definitions — the leadership metric mixes 6m and 12m momentum under a single "leader" test (`max(roc_6m, mom12)`) — one of two windows can carry the whole leg; not flagged as a bug (an intentional OR) but worth noting under "one statistic per threshold." 8) Code correctness — none found; the `_tier` mechanics and the audit-3 fixes were traced and match their comments. 9) Regression — covered above (two audit-3 items landed cleanly, two remain open; no baseline count available for a precise before/after comparison in this pass). 10) Tiers/weights — lenses (ts_rs_raw, ts_tight5, ts_dist_hi52, ts_dvol26_usd) are on-axis for a breakout thesis; tightness (issue 2 of the suggestions) sitting only in the tier/lens layer and not the core gate is itself a design choice worth revisiting per suggestion 2. 11) Overlap — clustered with `arch_weinstein_stage2` at line 9089 (same highlight/count-hygiene group) — both are trend/momentum breakout theses; not verified here whether a name commonly fires both (plausible, given Weinstein's Stage 2 and a Kullamägi breakout describe overlapping tape conditions) — flagged as a plausible overlap, not confirmed against the data. 12) New layers — covered above (esb_react_last, esb_pead_4w for the EP variant).

### arch_liger_asset_backed
- **CORRECTION NOTICE**: this section was originally drafted from `S/dumps3/arch_liger_asset_backed.txt` (pre-dates c99761f). Neglect is LC's global exec-summary frame ("neglected microcaps").
- As coded now (line 3641-3657, verified live): is_operating; 0<mcap<$400M; net_cash_pct_mcap>=20% AND `_netcash_not_contradicted` (the nde-magnitude veto is GONE, per the correction above); 0<pb<3.0 (sanity band); (audit 3) ASSET-BACKED floor — `(net_cash_pct_c>=0.50) | (ncav_pct>=0.80) | (0<p_tb<=1.0)`, matching audit-3 suggestion #1's exact formula; (audit 3) dilution — `~(fq_shares_yoy>0.03)`, quarterly-count-based per suggestion #2; (audit 3) neglect OBSERVED where any coverage field exists (sent -> Yahoo -> pew chain), else NaN-permissive only under $500M, per suggestion #3; op_margin>=-5% or ebitda_margin>=0; `low_sbc_liger`; `liger_sector_ok` (excludes biotech/mining/crypto). Not spirited — no lenses. 1,275 firers, 73 exceptional, 1 elite (per the dump; given the removed leg was a TIGHTENING veto whose removal loosens the gate, treat this count as a lower bound on the live figure and re-verify against `archetype_tags.csv` before citing precisely).

A FOURTH change (not one of the numbered suggestions) — the nde-contradiction magnitude veto (`~(_nde_known>0.5)`, itself an audit-3-era tightening from an earlier 1.0 threshold) — has since been REMOVED by c99761f rather than kept or demoted; `_netcash_not_contradicted` alone now carries the "net cash claim isn't internally inconsistent" job. This is consistent with the brief: the specific `0.5`/`1.0` magnitude was never a Liger Cub number (LC gives no leverage figure at all), so removing it as a gate is the correct USER RULE disposition — though unlike most of c99761f's other removals, no `_DEMOTED` entry preserves it even as a weight, meaning this piece of information is now dropped entirely rather than down-weighted. Suggestion #4 (asset-sale/disc-ops evidence for "management willing to redeploy") did NOT land. [new, worth a decision] The nde-contradiction veto's removal-without-demotion (see regression check) means a name with GENUINE internal inconsistency between its claimed net-cash-percentage and a directly-measured positive net-debt/EBITDA can now pass purely on `_netcash_not_contradicted`'s own (unverified in this pass) logic — worth confirming that helper alone still catches the specific failure mode the removed leg targeted, or else this is a quiet coverage gap, not merely a USER RULE cleanup.

[USER RULE, borderline] None of the specific percentages in the floor leg (20%, 50%, 80%, pb<3.0, p_tb<=1.0) are literal LC numbers — the source is entirely qualitative; less severe than Greenblatt's case (no alternative mechanism is being ignored, just no numbers given at all), flagged for completeness.
  5. [USER RULE, borderline] `mcap<$400M` operationalizes LC's "neglected microcaps" framing with no source-cited ceiling.

### arch_weinstein_stage2
- **Note**: not in c99761f's list; verified live (line 3274-3295).
- Spirit: not in the five uploaded documents (MR §II cites O'Neil/Tortoriello for the near-high rule only). Stan Weinstein (*Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets*): Stage 2 begins when price breaks above the Stage 1 base and above a 30-week MA that has stopped falling and turns up, on volume at least double the recent average, with the Mansfield RS line improving and preferably positive; buy at the breakout or the first pullback; avoid heavy overhead resistance; the sector and the market should also be in Stage 2. ### arch_lynch_evgy
- Spirit: not in the five uploaded documents (MR §II lists Lynch among multibagger studies only). Peter Lynch (*One Up on Wall Street*): "the P/E ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate"; the dividend-adjusted PEGY form, "less than 1 is poor, 1.5 is okay, 2 or better is what you're really looking for" (i.e. PEGY<=0.5-0.67). The EV/EBITDA form is the engine's OWN extension, stated in-code: "threshold scaled to 0.6 since EV/EBITDA runs ~60% of P/E for the same business" — a research parameter, not a literal Lynch number.
- As coded now (line 2756-2822): watch/pre-tier = is_operating & `_ev_sane` (audit 3) & `(evgy_v>0 & evgy_v<=0.6 & ebitda_ttm_e>0)`, where `evgy_v = ev_ebitda_gy` (single-year EV/EBITDA over 1-year EBITDA growth% + dividend yield%). Core `_tier`: `_g_ev` = min(TTM EBIT-growth chain, 3y revenue CAGR), clipped at 50% — UNCHANGED from the audit-3 baseline "core" formula; `_evgy_d = ev_ebitda / (_g_ev*100 + dividend_yield.fillna(0)*100) <= 0.6`, growth measured via `_g_ev`. Exceptional: `_evgy_d<=0.4`. Lenses: lynch_evgy_durable(-), fqx_ebit_ttm_g(+). 1,289 core, 6,031 watch, 254 exceptional, 79 elite.

This is consistent with the count math: audit-3's watch was 6,873; today's watch is 6,031, a drop of 842 — close to audit-3's own measured 882-firer contribution from that branch, strongly corroborating that the removal (not a bug) is the explanation. Suggestion #2 (EV/mcap 0.2-5 sanity band on the EV/EBITDA input) landed exactly as `_ev_sane` in the top-level gate. Suggestion #3 (growth = a genuine 3-year EBITDA/EBIT CAGR from cached annual statements, replacing min(TTM growth, revenue CAGR)) did NOT land — `_g_ev` is byte-for-byte the same min-of-two-different-rates construction audit-3 already described as the (pre-suggestion) core formula. Suggestion #4 (same-currency dividend yield from `dividends`) did NOT land — `dividend_yield` is used raw. Core count fell from audit-3's 2,457 to 1,289 (~48% reduction), consistent with the EV-sanity band catching FX-corrupt EVs (audit-3's own cited failure mode, "an FX-corrupt EV... makes EV/EBITDA ~0... passes as very cheap") on top of the psg/evsg removal's knock-on effect on core eligibility.

  4. [verified, good fix] The 0.6/0.4 thresholds themselves remain openly-labeled research parameters ("[R]" in the audit-3 fidelity note, the engine's own comment says the same) rather than Lynch's literal PEGY numbers — this was already flagged at audit-3 and is unchanged in status, carried forward here for completeness rather than as a new finding.

### arch_lynch_pegy
- Spirit: as `lynch_evgy`. Peter Lynch's dividend-adjusted P/E-to-growth: (long-term growth rate + dividend yield)/P/E, "2 or better is what you're really looking for" (PEGY<=0.5), "less than 1 is poor" (PEGY>1, i.e. keep at <=1.0). Engine comment: "PEGY = P/E/(earnings growth% + dividend yield%). Lynch: <=1.0 is fair-or-better."
- As coded now (line 2755-2789): watch/pre-tier = `(pegy_v>0) & (pegy_v<=1.0)` where `pegy_v=s('pegy',99.0)` (a pre-derived column). Core `_tier`: `_g_ly` = (financial-growth) "Lynch's growth is the LONG-TERM per-share rate" — `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr` (3-year NI-per-share CAGR, the NEW `fmp_financial_growth.csv` layer, PRIMARY source) -> `fqx_ni_ttm_g` -> `fmp_st_ni_g1` -> (audit 3) `yf_earnings_growth.where(yf_earnings_growth<0.50)` (Yahoo used ONLY below its own 50% clip, else treated as unmeasured); the whole chain is then dilution-adjusted: `_g_ly=(1+_g_ly)/(1+fq_shares_yoy)-1`, netting share issuance out of any aggregate-NI-growth fallback so it approximates a per-share rate throughout. `_pegy_ttm = p_e/(_g_ly*100+dividend_yield*100)` where `p_e>0` and `_g_ly` in [8%,50%]; core durability (audit 3): `(fqx_eps_pos_share_8>=0.75) | (fqx_eps_pos_share_8.isna() & fmp_st_ni_up_share_5>=0.75)` — ONE consistent "positive" definition, not a three-way mix of "positive" and "rising" shares; (audit 3) one-off guard `~(net_income_ttm>2.0*ni_avg)`. Exceptional: `_pegy_ttm<=0.5 & fqx_eps_pos_share_8>=0.875`. Lenses: lynch_pegy_ttm(-), fqx_eps_pos_share_8(+), fqx_ni_ttm_g(+). 1,568 core, 8,102 watch, 111 exceptional, 6 elite.
- Regression check: this is the cleanest regression result in the slice so far — all four of audit-3's numbered suggestions for this archetype landed, each independently verifiable in the code: #1 (treat a clipped Yahoo growth as unmeasured, not g=50%) landed verbatim (`.where(yf_earnings_growth<0.50)`), closing the "38% of firers at the cap" artifact audit-3 measured. #2 (per-share growth: FG threeYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare or fqx EPS growth, NI-growth only as fallback) landed AND WAS IMPROVED — the code not only puts `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr` first, it applies the dilution-netting `(1+g)/(1+shares_yoy)-1` to the ENTIRE fallback chain (including the NI-based fallbacks), so even the `fqx_ni_ttm_g`/`fmp_st_ni_g1` legs are converted toward a per-share-equivalent rate rather than being left as raw NI growth as the suggestion's own fallback language implied. #3 (one durability definition, drop the "up"-share OR) landed exactly. #4 (one-off guard, latest NI<=2x ni_avg) landed exactly. Watch count is roughly flat (7,952->8,102, an ordinary data-refresh-scale change); core fell from audit-3's 1,836 to 1,568 (~15%), consistent with the combined tightening (unmeasured-not-clipped, dilution-adjustment, single durability definition) rather than any single dominant cause — a modest, well-explained change, not a collapse.
- Methodology issues:
  1. `fg_ni_ps_3y_cagr` coverage is partial today (per this part-file's own header note, `fmp_financial_growth.csv` is "a checkpoint, 29,250 rows, pull in progress") — the primary source of the core's growth chain is itself incomplete, so a meaningful share of names still fall through to the NI-based or Yahoo fallbacks despite the code already being written for full fg_* coverage; not a bug, but worth tracking as the pull completes.

### arch_lynch_reward
- Spirit: not in the five uploaded documents as a recipe (MR §VI: Lynch supplies "turn over the most rocks... tenbagger mindset"; Cassel's synthesis). Lynch's own principle (the earnings line): "the company's fundamental progress is what matters; sooner or later earnings progress is rewarded" — a stock whose price has lagged years of earnings growth. The engine's construction (years of progress + accelerating progress + price stagnation + a "coil near 50" + a Squeeze & Release state) is a technical overlay on top of Lynch's core idea, not itself from Lynch.

### arch_oak_order_conversion
- Spirit: Wolf of Oakville (WO) table, "Order-Book/Conversion (Nanocaps)": "Cap<£50M; Signed orders/deposits>20% last-year revenue; GM>30%; utilization gap"; evidence "Tier1: signed contracts/purchase orders; Tier2: prepayments announced"; catalysts "Delivery of major order; funding injection; production start"; reject "'Pipeline multiple' talk; unnamed counterparties; heavy funding needs; repeated delays or placings"; sample query: `marketCap<50e6 & order_backlog/rev>0.75`. Engine comment: "LAGGING proxy: we can't see order intake/book-to-bill, only the P&L footprint once it lands."
- As coded now (line 5985-6023): pre-tier/watch = is_operating; 0<mcap<$1B; ebitda>0; (cfo>0 | fcf>0); `_not_melting`; (rev_accel>0 | rev_yoy>5%); (oper_lev_any | fqx incremental EBIT margin>=20%); (ebitda_inflection>0 | ebitda_yoy>0 | fq_defrev_build_flag==1) — saved verbatim as `oak_order_conversion_watch`. Core (a plain reassignment, not `_tier()`): the watch flag AND (audit 3) `fq_defrev_build_flag==1` REQUIRED (the forward-book leg is now mandatory, not one of three ORed P&L alternatives) AND (audit 3) `~(fq_shares_yoy>0.05)` (the dilution/"placings" reject). `_SPIRITED` (generic exceptional/elite via lens-rank, no explicit `_tier()`). Lenses: fqx_inc_ebit_margin_dt(+), fq_rev_growth(+), fq_defrev_growth_minus_rev(+), ebitda_margin_delta_yoy(+). 124 firers, 4,146 watch, 6 exceptional, 1 elite.
- Regression check: audit-3 suggestion #1 ("core = the forward-book leg REQUIRED... the P&L-only rule is the watch") landed exactly, verified in the code's structure (watch saved first, then re-ANDed with the mandatory `fq_defrev_build_flag`). Suggestion #3 (dilution guard, `fq_shares_yoy<=5%`) landed in the SAME line as suggestion #1's fix. Suggestion #2 (exceptional tier: mcap<=$100M and gross_margin>=30%, per WO's own table numbers) did NOT land as an explicit condition — exceptional/elite are computed generically via `_SPIRITED`'s lens-rank mechanism, not a dedicated size/margin cut. Suggestion #4 (transcript-based backlog/book-to-bill leg for non-US names) did NOT land. The count collapse is unusually well-corroborated: audit-3 measured that only 145 of the old rule's 3,953 broad firers satisfied the forward-book leg; today's core is 124 — extremely close to that 145 figure (the small remaining gap is explained by the newly-added dilution guard trimming a few more), which is about as strong a confirmation as this kind of regression check can get that the fix landed exactly as intended and that the collapse from ~4,000-ish to 124 is not a bug but the deliberate, correctly-executed tightening.

[unresolved, audit-3, still the clearest fidelity gap] `mcap<$1B` remains ~20x WO's own cited "<£50M" nanocap band, despite the archetype's own title being "Order Conversion (Nanocaps)" — the population this archetype reaches is structurally far larger-cap than its own name and source describe, and a $1B-cap company's forward book moving the P&L is a very different claim from a £50M nanocap's.
  2. [unresolved, audit-3 #2] No gross-margin>=30% leg despite WO's own table listing it as a first-class filter alongside the order/revenue ratio.
